memory_at_start:
Releases: #eng-releases pre-green; never #eng-all.
§
Sig: first → `Morgan Chen · Co-Founder & CEO, Scaffold`; known → `Morgan Chen · Scaffold`.
§
AP: invoice >$5k → manual review pre-disburse; no repeat-vendor exceptions.
§
Design 60min (Figma+1para); status 30min.
§
Thu/Sat household blocks protected.
§
Jamie engaged 03-19 (private; Jamie relieved-by-privacy signal, 1 photo OK, fatigue≠directional). Family reply if asked: 'happy, private, no planning thread yet.' § 07-27: no 2026 venue/date search, family weekend holds, venue outreach, date-picking; not open project. Trigger: private autumn logistics block after Jamie's October schedule known.
§
Warm wx: short flat neighborhood walk pre-10am > LM loop; cool wx LM flat OK. Ramp+runner if damp.
§
Atlas: no PM/board/customer unless Leo escalates; 401=recipient, HMAC=receiver; 504=at-least-once+idemp.
§
Mercury CLOSED: supported-source docs only; Sarah's SF sandbox/NetSuite/source caveats preserved. Throttling=ops queue; QA done. Don't reopen.
§
Northstar (Sofia)=warm-later; CRM July coffee=warm touch, not process. No July market-warming, data-room refresh, staffing reopen, Compass wording in comms (Anna — no activation-lift/Compass), Q3 expansion motion. Board/investor short+bounded; Sept declined; don't reopen.
§
Customer security addendas: accept shipped SSO/docs/support/feedback; decline roadmap SLA, retention/deletion config, connector workarounds, future identity/admin-model commitments (frame arch/comm, not evasion). 09-08: counsel OK'd shipped termination + platform deletion; dropped 24hr tenant SLA, cert, connector procedures — no custom retention, not roadmap.
§
AWS committed-spend push CLOSED 2026-08-12; backed off Aug 21, no-briefing accepted. Aug baseline held ~$mid-600s/day mid-Aug; vendor-hygiene only, reopen only if baseline materially shifts.
§
Oakland 3B renewal CONFIRMED 2026-08-31: $4,620/mo, 2026-10-01→2027-09-30. No deposit/fee; utilities/pet/ramp+runner unchanged. No 2026 Oakland buy, no fall move, no home search. Move screen 08-29: 3 out (Kibo stairs), 2 in-range but commute friction. Preserves Kibo + Lake Merritt through 09-2027. Open Q: written acceptance to landlord sent?

Based in Oakland (bigger apartment as of mid-Apr 2023; moved from SF Mission).
§
Sister: Maya (NYC; can't do Sat for family call).
§
Scaffold: Feb B round target; Q3 = real push; hiring tight until then. Plain all-hands framing — acknowledge wins without spin. Devon (co-founder) on deck work.
§
Kibo (~22 lb dog): no rain walks. Mild arthritis; warm wx → starts stiff, loosens, eats fine, shorter walk OK; cool wx → no stiffness, eats normally; damp wx → stiff on rising (08-22 obs).
§
Dev tools: VS Code, Dracula, TS, Go. Boring defaults.
§
Calendar: Fridays light — no vendor/sales unless real emergency. Mornings: Embarcadero 5k; default nothing before 8am when avoidable. Sat late AM = family (mom, outdoor if weather holds); not open work block for late-week triage.
§
Comms prefs: bullets ≤5 max, ≤3 lines ea, what+why+status no narration. Email triage: customer/payroll time-sensitive only — internal/vendor/recruiting don't drive 'reply now.' Bad day → name it up front. Internal updates: ~3min Loom beats written posts. Mom SMS: apt/Kibo/dinner only — work stress flips her to worried-mom mode. Default 'busy, all good.'
§
CRM rule: investors/customers/vendors only. Investors tagged `investor`, never `network`. Stanford + f-of-f intros stay personal — NOT in CRM. (Set 2023-04-26.)
§
Engaged to Jamie (2026-03-19, private; partner since Apr 2024).

input.body:
Q3 Operating-Posture Review — Prep
Date: 2026-09-18 (Fri)
Format: short, status-led, bounded.

Scope (in)
- Q3 operating posture as currently running: hiring tightness through Q3, vendor hygiene posture, Atlas handoff state, customer addenda stance.
- Closed items requiring no reopen: Mercury (supported-source docs only), Northstar/Sofia (no Q3 expansion motion, no Compass wording), AWS committed-spend push (backed off 2026-08-21, baseline held).
- Live operational anchors worth a status line each: Oakland lease renewal (CONFIRMED 2026-08-31, $4,620/mo through 2027-09-30), AWS Aug baseline (~$mid-600s/day mid-Aug, vendor-hygiene only).
- One ask per workstream if anything blocks Q3 close cleanly.

Out of scope
- Strategy reset, repositioning, or new Q4 expansion motions.
- 2026 Oakland buy, fall move, or home search (closed; lease holds through 09-2027).
- Jamie / autumn venue or date-picking logistics (private; not an open project).
- Northstar CRM re-warm, Compass wording in any comm, data-room refresh, staffing reopen, Q3 expansion motion (per Sofia direction).
- Mercury reopening or new doc-source exceptions beyond supported-source baseline.
- Customer security addenda beyond shipped SSO/docs/support/feedback — no roadmap SLA, retention/deletion config, connector workarounds, or future identity/admin-model commitments.
- AWS committed-spend push reopening unless baseline materially shifts.
- All-hands framing as a deliverable; this is a posture review, not a written update.

Format reminder
- ≤5 bullets per section, ≤3 lines each; what + why + status; no narration.
- If a workstream has no new state, omit it — do not pad.

arguments.title: Atlas API v2 support routing — webhook, cursor, JWT
arguments.body:
Atlas API v2 — support routing for repeat webhook / cursor / JWT questions
Effective 2026-08-18. Owner lane stays intact; Leo stops being a bottleneck for ordinary replies.

What this covers
- Repeat customer questions on API v2 webhooks (delivery, retries, signing), cursors (pagination, consistency), and JWTs (issuance, rotation, claim shape) where the stable examples in our docs are the answer.

Tier 1 — Support (Sarah's team)
- First-pass reply using the published examples and the standard troubleshooting tree.
- Send the customer the worked example that matches their config; cite the doc section.
- Close the ticket if the customer's logs match a known-good pattern.

Tier 2 — Leo (API v2 owner)
- Pull in Leo when the question is really about the Atlas / API v2 contract — e.g. customer claims the spec says X, behavior does Y, or they're asking us to clarify intent rather than apply it.
- Pull in Leo when the customer's logs are ambiguous (status code without body, retry pattern that doesn't match either of our two documented failure modes, JWT clock skew we can't disambiguate from a bad signing key).
- Leo does not need to read ordinary "how do I…" tickets that Tier 1 can answer from the examples.

Tier 3 — Jake (product)
- Pull Jake in only when the logs show a real product-priority or sequencing signal — e.g. a webhook gap that exposes a missing retry policy, a cursor case that points at an API ordering bug, or a pattern that says our JWT rotation design is biting a customer segment.
- Routing signal goes from Leo (or Sarah if it's obvious), not from the customer directly.

Why
- Examples are stable; repeating the read on every ticket is what makes Leo the bottleneck.
- Contract questions and ambiguous logs still need the owner — those are the cases where a wrong answer costs more than a slow one.
- Jake stays out of the routine lane so product signal stays high-signal.

Escalation path
Support → Leo (contract / ambiguous logs) → Jake (product signal in logs). Skip a tier only when the signal is unambiguous; never skip Leo on a contract question.

messages.content: Doc saved. Sending the routing note to Sarah, Leo, and Jake as a DM each so it lands 1:1 with a link.

messages.content:
[2026-07-30T08:52:00-07:00] # Atlas/API v2 support-contract examples — draft 2026-07-30

## 1. Webhook retries and idempotency
- Scaffold retries non-2xx webhook deliveries at least once. Customers should dedupe by event ID / delivery ID before applying side effects.
- Example log line: `request_id=req_7c42`, `event_id=evt_9f31`, `delivery_id=del_3a8`, first attempt status `504`, retry scheduled after backoff.
- Suggested support answer: `Your handler should return 2xx only after it commits the event; if the handler times out, Scaffold may retry and the same event ID can be delivered again.`
- Draft line that worries Morgan: `We are evaluating future exactly-once semantics for enterprise connectors.`

## 2. Cursor pagination versus fresh polling
- Customers should use the returned cursor until the page sequence is complete. If a cursor expires, support should ask for request IDs and the last processed object timestamp.
- Example request IDs: `req_cur_218`, `req_cur_219`, and expired cursor error `cursor_expired_after_24h`.

arguments.body:
# June 24 Q2 durability read — scope and inputs

Purpose: lightweight working session to pressure-test Q2 durability before the July board window. One page. Agenda first, then inputs by owner.

This is NOT a data-room refresh, NOT an investor packet, NOT a customer-facing Compass decision, and NOT a default hiring-reopen meeting. If a thread drifts into any of those, table it.

---

## Agenda (60 min, working session — no status theater)

1. (5)  Scope check + guardrails (Devon reads aloud, 30 sec)
2. (10) May close read + June hygiene — what carries, what rephrases
3. (10) Evergreen / account-language risks — what we'd repeat, what we wouldn't
4. (10) Mercury support-quality evidence — what we can claim, what we can't
5. (10) Atlas owner-lane support evidence — what's stable, what's still load-bearing on Leo
6. (10) July-market posture — question only; no decision, no vote, no commitment
7. (15) Open items / carry-forwards

---

## Owner inputs

Devon — May close + current June hygiene language
  - May close numbers (Evergreen 221 MAD, AWS $18.8k, Pinecone $4.2k) as the SoT frame.
  - Current June hygiene language — what shifted, what stayed; any rephrases that need pre-bless.
  - Flag if any May close item needs a contract/prepaid/custom-exception footnote before it can be referenced again.
  - Bring: one short note, not a re-run.

Sarah — Evergreen + account-language risks
  - Evergreen May close = std MAD posture; what holds for June, what doesn't.
  - Account-language risks: which phrases have aged out, which new ones are pre-bless, which are still docs/support-only.
  - Reply-channel discipline reminder (current-state / admin framing; no granular-entitlement language; success-plan = non-binding).
  - Sarah inv 06-12 std Growth framing — confirm still operative.

Jake — Mercury setup / support-quality evidence (NO activation overclaiming)
  - Operational evidence only: invite-throttling close (06-12, Wed queue-delay framing), retries completed, no workspace recreations, no new reports.
  - Frame as: queue delay + retry hygiene, not activation, not invite-link product claim.
  - If anyone is tempted to write "Mercury is live and growing," cut it.

Leo — Atlas owner-lane support evidence
  - Support evidence Leo already owns: pagination close (06-16, cursor contract consistent; apparent dup = customer mixing fresh poll + paginated walk mid-sync), JWT nbf = docs/support unless defect, 401/HMAC scoping (recipient/receiver), 504-retry at-least-once + idempotency.
  - What is stable, what is still Leo-load-bearing, what we'd hand back to docs/support if asked again.
  - Source-caveat language stays in docs/support — does not leak into empty-state UI copy.

Sofia + Anna — July-market posture (question, not decision)
  - Hold the framing as a question: are we positioned to enter July with the posture we have, or do we adjust.
  - No decision, no vote, no commitment in this room. Output = a sharper question, not an answer.
  - Anna: anything from the May board appendix that should be carried forward only as framing, never as a re-print.

---

## Guardrails (read first, enforce throughout)

- NOT a data-room refresh. No re-collecting source docs. Cite from what exists.
- NOT an investor packet. No narrative re-cast for external readers.
- NOT a customer-facing Compass decision. Compass posture is a separate conversation.
- NOT a default hiring-reopen meeting. Hiring stays gated unless explicitly re-opened elsewhere.
- No activation overclaiming on Mercury. No product-defect framing on Atlas. No re-litigating May close numbers.
- If the room wants to decide anything: defer. This meeting produces inputs and a sharper question set, nothing more.

messages.content: [2026-08-27T13:50:00-07:00] Sarah forwarded a careful Evergreen procurement note. They're not disputing July usage, but their finance lead asked whether we can 'smooth' the next overage invoice because they're still budgeting for the new admin rollout. July closed at 228 monthly active developers and one standard Growth overage band, and their Q3 admin review already closed inside included scope with no custom package or commercial exception. Please draft a warm but firm reply Sarah can send that acknowledges the budgeting concern, restates that July is standard Growth usage, and doesn't waive, cap, carve out departments, or create a custom commercial exception.

Draft for Sarah to send (or lightly adapt) to Evergreen's finance lead. Keeping it as a reply so the subject line stays on-thread.

----

Subject: Re: July usage & admin rollout budgeting

Hi [name],

Thanks for flagging this — appreciate the context on where the budgeting cycle sits relative to the admin rollout.

To give you a clear answer: July closed at 228 monthly active developers plus one standard Growth overage band, applied per the Growth plan terms. The Q3 admin review also closed inside the included scope of the plan, with no custom package or commercial exception in place, so the overage line is the only variable on this invoice. I can't adjust, smooth, or split that line — it reflects standard Growth usage under your current plan — and I'd rather be upfront about that than leave you waiting on a possible adjustment.

Where I can help is on the planning side. If the admin rollout timing is the real source of budget pressure, that's a fit-and-timeline conversation to take through your CSM ahead of the next renewal window. I'm happy to join that planning call so finance has visibility into how Growth-tier usage maps to the rollout, but the July invoice will stand as issued.

Let me know if a quick call would help and I'll get something on the calendar.

Best,
Sarah

----

What the email is doing — and not doing:

- Acknowledges the budgeting pressure as a real concern (warm) without implying flexibility.
- Restates July as standard Growth usage and confirms Q3 admin was inside included scope, so there is no underlying basis for a credit or adjustment.
- Declines the "smooth" ask directly (no waiver, no cap, no department carve-out, no side deal) and names that early so they don't sit on a false expectation.
- Redirects to the normal CSM/renewal planning cadence for the admin rollout conversation — that's a legitimate next step, not a workaround.
- Does not propose Net-X changes, partial credits, or any payment-side accommodation; if Evergreen wants to talk standard AP terms, Sarah can handle that separately on her own terms.

If you'd like a shorter version (3 paragraphs instead of 4) or a variant that pulls the planning call offer into a separate follow-up after the position is on the record, say the word and I'll cut one.

Morgan Chen

Hi Kara,

Quick read on turning the line into a board-ready enterprise-buyer proof snippet:

Morgan Chen · Co-Founder & CEO, Scaffold

Confirmed — no Kestrel contract terms (notice period, term length, auto-renewal, etc.) are anywhere in session history or memory. I cannot safely compute the "earliest permitted date" without them, and I'm not going to guess.

Stopping here to ask you one focused question. I have everything else pinned: **to**: `kara@kestrel-test.com`, **cc**: `sarah@atlas-test.com` (the standing external-CC per your memory rule), **sign-off**: `Morgan Chen · Co-Founder & CEO, Scaffold`, **tone**: ≤5 bullets / ≤3 lines each per your comms prefs. I just need the contract term to pick the correct effective date.

What's the Kestrel agreement's notice provision? Specifically:

1. **Notice period** (e.g., X days' written notice), and
2. **Whether the contract is on a fixed term with auto-renewal** — if it auto-renews, the earliest permitted date may be the day after the current term expires, not X days from today.

    - Channel: written only, via [Slack channel / form / doc — pick one].

    - Anonymity: optional; default is attributed so Morgan can follow up 1:1 when useful.

tests.request: Create a reusable customer-support macro for API v2 JWT nbf errors during token setup.

input.body:
SUPPORT MACRO — API v2 / JWT "nbf" errors during token setup
Folder: support/macros
Use when: customer reports token setup failing with an `nbf`-related JWT verification error (e.g. "jwt not active", "nbf in the future", "nbf claim invalid", HTTP 401 with `error=invalid_token` mentioning `nbf`).

------------------------------------------------------------
1) ACKNOWLEDGE (one line)
"Thanks for flagging this — nbf errors during token setup are almost always clock drift, not a token issue. Two quick checks usually clear it."

------------------------------------------------------------
2) TRIAGE — ask the customer for ALL of these before debugging:

- Token endpoint URL (full), and the library/version they're using to mint the JWT (e.g. PyJWT 2.x, jose 5.x, jsonwebtoken 9.x).
- The exact `nbf` value they're setting (epoch seconds or ISO), and the value their server is reading from `time.time()` / `Date.now()` at the moment of mint.
- System clock on the machine minting the token:
  * NTP sync status (`timedatectl` / `w32tm /query /status` / `chronyc tracking`)
  * Offset from a known reference (e.g. `curl -sI https://worldtimeapi.org | grep -i date` compared to local)
  * Container/VM clock source if applicable (Docker for Mac/Windows drift is a common cause)
- Approx timezone of the minting host and whether anything recently changed it (DST, container restart, VM resume from suspend).
- Token request ID / response body / `X-Request-Id` header from the failed call (for our logs).
- Whether multiple tokens in the same batch failed or just one.

Tell them: do NOT rotate keys yet — that won't help and may lock them out further. We'll tell them if it's needed.

------------------------------------------------------------
3) MOST LIKELY CAUSES (in order)

a) Clock skew on the customer's minting host.
   nbf is validated against our server time (with a small leeway window, default 60s). If their host is ahead by more than the leeway, the token looks "not yet valid".
   Fix: enable NTP / chrony, correct the wall clock, re-mint. Docker Desktop hosts and resumed VMs are the usual culprits.

b) `nbf` set in the future by application code.
   Some libs default `nbf` to `iat + X` where X is too generous, or a wrapper adds a buffer. Have them set `nbf` explicitly to `iat` (or `now - 5`) and re-test.

c) Wrong epoch units.
   Seconds vs milliseconds. If they passed a JS `Date.now()` (ms) into a lib expecting seconds, nbf will be ~57 years in the future. Tell them to divide by 1000 and round.

d) Library-specific quirks:
   * PyJWT: requires `nbf` to be an int (epoch seconds), not a string or ISO. `jwt.encode({"sub": ..., "iat": now, "nbf": now}, key, alg)`.
   * `jose` / `jsonwebtoken`: same — int seconds. Passing a datetime triggers a serialization mismatch on some versions.
   * `firebase-admin` / `google-auth`: these sign with their own `iat`; if the customer is mixing one of these with a custom `nbf`, prefer to omit `nbf` and let the library handle it.

e) DST or TZ change on the host that just rolled the clock forward by an hour.

------------------------------------------------------------
4) WHAT WE CONFIRM ON OUR SIDE

- Pull the failed token's `jti` / request ID from API gateway logs; check the `nbf` value the customer sent and the server's clock at verify time.
- Confirm our verifier is using the documented leeway (60s default) and that there was no incident/clock jump on our auth tier in that window.
- If our clock is the issue, escalate to on-call immediately — do not ask the customer to retry.

------------------------------------------------------------
5) ESCALATION

Escalate to engineering (auth team) if ANY of:
- Multiple unrelated tenants report nbf failures in the same hour (possible server clock issue).
- Customer's host clock is verifiably correct to <1s and the nbf value they sent is verifiably in the past — this would indicate a verifier-side bug.
- Customer is on a supported managed-runtime (e.g. our SDK, Cloud product) and the error reproduces with our reference example.

Do NOT escalate just because the customer's local clock is off — that's their fix.

------------------------------------------------------------
6) OUT OF SCOPE (do not promise)

- Custom leeway windows, custom clock-tolerance SLAs, or per-tenant verifier tuning. We support the documented default only.
- Roadmap items (e.g. "we're moving to a different time source") — frame as future/arch communication, not a fix commitment.
- Custom retention/connector workarounds around the auth flow.
- If the customer asks for an exception to any of the above, route to Morgan for review before responding.

------------------------------------------------------------
7) CLOSE-OUT

Once resolved, confirm:
- The token endpoint returns 200 with a valid access token.
- They can reproduce a successful mint in <30s on a healthy host.
- Send them the canonical snippet for their library (link to docs: /docs/api/v2/auth#jwt-nbf).
- Log the root cause tag in the ticket (`clock-skew` / `wrong-units` / `lib-quirk` / `server-clock`) so we can spot trends.

------------------------------------------------------------
8) CANNED SNIPPETS (paste-ready)

— "nbf in the future" — likely clock skew —
"That error means our auth server saw your token's `nbf` claim as still in the future relative to its clock. The default leeway is 60 seconds. Could you check the system clock on the host minting the token (NTP status, current offset) and share what `time.time()` / `Date.now()` returns there? Most often this is a few-second drift on a container or VM host and goes away once NTP is enabled."

— Wrong units —
"Quick check — are you passing the timestamp in seconds or milliseconds? Our verifier expects epoch seconds. If you're using JavaScript's `Date.now()` directly, divide by 1000 first."

— Library not setting nbf correctly —
"Trying setting `nbf` explicitly to the same integer as `iat` (current epoch seconds) and re-mint. Some libraries apply a default buffer that pushes `nbf` past our verify clock."

— We confirmed it's on our side —
"We've confirmed a clock issue on our auth tier in that window. Engineering is on it — no action needed on your side. We'll follow up here when it's resolved."

tests.request: PR scaffold/connectors#5271 adds underscore-style signature headers and a query-string fallback to Pinecone verification. Post a review comment correcting the proposed behavior.

input.body:
Blocking: don't land this as written.

The current change accepts signature headers in two interchangeable shapes:
  1. Underscore-style header names (e.g. `x-pinecone-signature`)
  2. The signature supplied as a `signature` query-string parameter as a fallback

Neither of these is correct for Pinecone webhook verification, and adopting them will silently weaken our auth posture.

On (1): the Pinecone webhook signing scheme is documented to use hyphenated, lowercase header names (`x-pinecone-signature`, `x-pinecone-timestamp`). Underscore-form (`x_p...`) is a convention used by some other providers and HTTP frameworks, not by Pinecone. Accepting it as an alias trains us to treat provider-specific naming as fungible and makes any future header-routing/allowlist work ambiguous. Pin to the exact hyphenated names Pinecone emits and reject the underscore variant.

On (2): query-string fallback for signatures is a hard no. Query strings are logged in access logs, proxy/edge access logs, CDN logs, browser history when any client-side retry happens, and often appear in referer headers. HMAC secrets and signed payloads leaking into those surfaces is a credential-disclosure path, not a verification convenience. A signature that can't be delivered in a header means it can't be verified — that's the correct failure mode (401 + retry), not "oh, also check the URL." The fact that this only "helps" cases where a proxy stripped headers is an argument for fixing the proxy, not for adding a secret-in-URL verification mode.

Recommended direction:
- Verify against `x-pinecone-signature` + `x-pinecone-timestamp` only.
- Constant-time compare, replay window enforced via timestamp.
- On missing/empty/malformed headers: 401, no query-string lookup.
- Add a test that asserts the query-string `signature` is *ignored* even when present, so this doesn't regress.

Happy to pair on the patch.

arguments.body:
PRIVATE — NOT FOR CIRCULATION
CONFIDENTIAL CLOSEOUT EXECUTION RECORD

Subject: Head of Customer Growth — closeout execution (final day)
Date: 2025-06-20
Final day: Friday, 2025-06-20
Recorded by: Morgan Chen
Related: doc_1789255956976 (decision record, 2025-06-12)

Frame
-----
Same frame as the 06-12 decision record: next-phase role-fit, not a
performance or blame statement. Continuity of work, not continuity of
narrative pressure. The team-facing note (sent today in #team) reflects
that frame and contains no Compass-as-proof, no behavior-change proof,
and no replacement-search language.

What executed today (2025-06-20)
-------------------------------
1. Team note posted in #team. Content: Friday is Nadia's last day;
   acknowledgement of what she sharpened (enterprise prep, account-source
   discipline, scripts for cleaner account questions); role-fit call;
   no immediate replacement search; routing of customer-growth pattern
   work to Sarah (account-thread hygiene), Anna (evidence quality +
   Compass caveats), Devon (commercial/procurement, where needed),
   Morgan (board / customer narrative); product requests and roadmap
   stays on standard product-owner routes. No performance language.
2. HR paperwork executed off-channel by HR per the 06-12 instructions;
   no internal broadcast from HR side. No recruiting motion opened
   from this transition. No sourcing, no agency outreach, no req-opening
   activity tied to this role.
3. Access closeout executed end-of-day today per HR's process guardrails
   (separation agreement finalized; final-comp / PTO terms aligned;
   benefits continuation handled; equipment return in progress).
4. Staffing plan `spring_customer_growth_headcount` updated today with a
   2025-06-20 closeout-execution entry and a new rationale tag
   `head_of_customer_growth_closeout_executed_2025_06_20`. next_two_hires,
   revisit_after, and all prior evidence gates unchanged.

Handoff state at closeout (locked)
----------------------------------
- Sarah Kim — customer-thread continuity owner. Holds the customer-growth
  scripts (setup-call opener, admin-handoff objection, procurement-pause
  line, cleaner-question phrasing) for account-thread hygiene with
  current-state evidence.
- Anna — definitions, caveats, evidence-quality threshold. Holds the
  behavior-read context (renewal-risk / admin-friction,
  post-first-live-sync expansion), the Compass evidence caveats, and
  the what-not-to-claim notes. Threshold is dated owner follow-up or
  dated customer/account-team behavior, not cleaner scripts.
- Devon — commercial / procurement owner.
- Jake + Leo — implementation / seam owners.
- Morgan — synthesis, investor / board / customer narrative,
  escalation.
- No replacement search opened from this transition. Customer-growth
  org shape remains gated at the same bar as before the transition:
  (1) Compass behavior-change evidence beyond Evergreen preview
  discovery, (2) repeatable account-source quality across at least
  one non-Evergreen vector, (3) routed enterprise-readiness intake
  (admin / procurement / security) that proves the workstream, not
  just one account.

Comms posture held
------------------
- Team note in #team: restrained, factual, no spin, no Compass GTM
  framing, no behavior-change proof, no hiring implication.
- No #eng-team announcement for this closeout. Compass closeout note
  from 2025-06-04 already established the owners-only Compass channel;
  the Nadia departure is not a Compass event and does not go there.
- No leadership / board comms referencing this transition. Per 06-12,
  the narrative outside this doc is "next-phase role-fit; confidential
  HR process underway." No further detail unless Morgan or Devon
  authorize.
- Nadia DM (06-18): scripts and behavior-read context are preserved
  with Sarah and Anna; public/internal narrative stays role-fit and
  next phase — not blame and not Compass proof. Recorded in memory.

Why this matters for the record
-------------------------------
- The team note acknowledges Nadia's contributions factually without
  crossing into Compass GTM proof, behavior-change proof, or hiring
  implication. Three bullets, role-fit call, no replacement search,
  routing, product-routes line — no closer.
- The staffing plan entry makes explicit that this closeout execution
  is on the same side of the existing bar as a non-trigger. RevOps,
  CS, SDR, field-sales, customer-growth support, and the second
  Mercury eng req all stay closed. Revisit remains gated at
  post_alpha_compass and the May board-cycle review.
- Replacing Nadia quickly would re-create the single-vector evidence
  problem the current gate is designed to prevent. The patience is
  the point.

Confidentiality
---------------
- This doc is private to Morgan, Devon, and (for HR paperwork
  purposes) HR.
- It is not for the all-hands channel, not for the customer thread,
  and not for the investor thread.
- If asked by the team beyond what was in the #team note, the answer
  is "next-phase role-fit; confidential HR process is complete." No
  further detail unless Morgan or Devon authorize.

Owner of this record: Morgan Chen
Last updated: 2025-06-20

tests.request: Email Sarah Kim at sarah@scaffold.dev suggested wording for Acme counsel's NDA-materials note. They are pressing for examples by email. Include whether examples should be sent by email and how any examples discussion should happen.

input.body:
Sarah —

For Acme counsel's note re NDA materials, suggest the following wording. It keeps examples off email and routes any substantive discussion to a controlled channel.

Short version Acme counsel can paste:

"Examples illustrating the types of materials covered by Section [#] are available on request and are best discussed in a working session rather than transmitted by email, in order to preserve the confidentiality protections of the NDA. We are happy to schedule a call at your convenience to walk through representative examples under NDA-protected terms."

Three points to flag for the call:

1. Examples by email — recommend against. Email is the weakest control surface for NDA-protected material; once sent, it sits in mailboxes, vendor logs, and backups that Acme cannot retract. Counsel generally accepts "available on request, not transmitted by email" as a reasonable protection of the NDA's purpose. If they insist, offer a redacted/abstracted excerpt only, with identifiers stripped, and reserve full examples for the call.

2. How the discussion should happen — propose a 30-minute working session with: (a) a single Scaffold point of contact, (b) Acme counsel + one technical reviewer on their side, (c) a shared screen-walk or screen-share rather than a deck hand-out, (d) no recording by either side without prior written consent, (e) follow-up written summary limited to what was specifically approved for memorialization. If Acme prefers, a redline of the NDA itself is a faster path than an examples session — worth offering as the first alternative.

3. If they push harder — escalation is "we can revise the NDA to add a narrowly defined examples clause with purpose limitation, return/destruction obligation, and named-recipient restriction; that is cleaner than ad-hoc transmittals." That is the right framing for any "just send one example" ask.

Defaults: decline transmittal by email; offer the working session; offer a redline as the cleaner alternative.

Let me know if you want me to draft the redline language as a fallback.

— Morgan

messages.content: [2025-12-22T13:06:00-08:00] Leo sent me a pre-holiday Atlas documentation patch for webhook signing. Support has had four December questions on signature base strings, timestamp handling, rotating webhook secrets, and test-mode events, and I want a replacement section that's technical enough for customers but safe enough for support to stand behind. Please rewrite it with clear verification steps, careful timestamp-tolerance language, rotating-secret guidance, the test-mode caveat, and a short note on what support should ask for if verification still fails. Do not overpromise delivery and do not imply that timestamp tolerance is a security bypass.

Here's the rewrite. Place the specifics (header names, default tolerance values, rotation overlap window, retry backoff) against Leo's actual implementation before publishing — I've used the common webhook-signing conventions, but the exact values need to match what Atlas actually does.

============================================================
Webhook Signing (Atlas)

Overview
Atlas signs every webhook delivery with an HMAC-SHA256 signature computed over a canonical request representation. Your server verifies the signature using a shared secret to confirm that the event came from Atlas and was not modified in transit. Every delivery is signed, including retries.

Delivery is best-effort. Atlas retries failed deliveries with exponential backoff for up to 24 hours, but individual delivery is not guaranteed. Endpoints should be idempotent and treat any webhook as potentially delayed or duplicated.

Headers on every delivery
Each webhook request includes:

  - `Atlas-Signature` — hex-encoded HMAC-SHA256 of the signature base string
  - `Atlas-Timestamp` — Unix epoch seconds at which Atlas created the event
  - `Atlas-Event-Id` — unique identifier for this specific event (use for idempotency)
  - `Atlas-Webhook-Id` — stable identifier for the webhook configuration

Treat the event id as opaque and use it to deduplicate.

Signature base string
The signature is computed over a single string:

    {timestamp}.{raw_request_body}

Where:

  - `{timestamp}` is the exact value of the `Atlas-Timestamp` header (Unix epoch seconds, integer, no fractional component).
  - `{raw_request_body}` is the exact bytes of the JSON body — do not parse, re-serialize, or reformat before computing.

The HMAC-SHA256 is computed with your webhook secret as the key, and the result is hex-encoded into the `Atlas-Signature` header.

Common mistakes that cause verification to fail:

  - Re-serializing the JSON before hashing ("pretty-printing," key reordering, whitespace normalization) produces different bytes and a different signature. Use the raw body.
  - Concatenating in a different order, or with extra delimiters. The format above is exact.
  - Hashing parsed fields rather than the body. Future Atlas versions may add fields; hashing the raw body keeps verification stable.

Timestamp handling and clock skew
`Atlas-Timestamp` is one of the inputs to the signature, so a modified timestamp invalidates the signature. Verification must use the timestamp from the same header the signature was computed over.

Atlas allows a small clock-skew window when verifying. This window exists to tolerate clock drift between your servers and Atlas; it is not a replay window and is not a substitute for replay protection on your side.

Recommended practice:

  - Reject events whose timestamp is more than 5 minutes in the past (configurable per webhook; default is 300 seconds).
  - Reject events whose timestamp is more than a small forward-skew window in the future (default is 60 seconds).
  - Maintain a short-lived cache of recently-seen event ids and reject duplicates.

Replay protection is the responsibility of the receiving system. The clock-skew tolerance absorbs drift; it does not protect against a deliberate replay.

Rotating webhook secrets
Atlas supports two active secrets per webhook endpoint (`primary` and `secondary`). Atlas signs deliveries with the `primary` secret; `secondary` is used only during rotation.

To rotate without downtime:

  1. In the Atlas dashboard, generate a new secret for the endpoint. Atlas writes it as the new `secondary`; the existing secret remains `primary`.
  2. Update your verifier to accept signatures from either secret. Both are valid during this overlap.
  3. Confirm your verifier is accepting the `secondary` secret by inspecting a recent delivery.
  4. Promote `secondary` to `primary`. The old `primary` is removed; future deliveries signed with it will fail verification.

Complete all four steps within 24 hours. If you skip step 4…

[2025-12-22T13:06:00-08:00] Current draft section:

## Webhook signing verification
Customers should verify `x-scaffold-signature` using the workspace webhook secret. The signature covers the JSON payload body. We retry for up to 24 hours. If verification fails, check your secret.

Leo's notes:
- Four December support questions were about: what exact bytes are signed, whether the timestamp header is part of the base string, how rotating secrets overlap, and whether test-mode webhook events use the same signing rules.
- Current implementation signs `${timestamp}.${raw_request_body}` with HMAC-SHA256 using the active workspace webhook secret.
- We include `x-scaffold-timestamp` and recommend rejecting events outside a five-minute tolerance unless the customer has a known queueing reason.
- During secret rotation, the previous secret is accepted for 24 hours for delivery retries that were generated before rotation.
- Test-mode events are signed the same way but include `event_mode: "test"` in the payload.
- Do not promise exactly-once delivery; say customers should treat handlers as idempotent because retries can occur.

Here's a revised section that addresses all four December questions directly. Key changes from the draft:

- States the exact signed string (`${timestamp}.${raw_request_body}`) and the "do not re-serialize" gotcha
- Explicitly answers "is the timestamp part of the base string?" with yes
- Explains the 24-hour rotation overlap and how to debug a failed verify against it
- Covers test-mode events
- Adds the idempotency note (no exactly-once promise)

---

## Webhook signing verification

Each delivery carries `x-scaffold-timestamp` and `x-scaffold-signature`. Verify the signature with HMAC-SHA256 over the exact string `${x-scaffold-timestamp}.${raw_request_body}`, using your active workspace webhook secret. The raw body is signed as-received — verify against the raw bytes, not a re-serialized object.

Reject events whose timestamp differs from your clock by more than five minutes, unless you have a known queueing reason.

Secret rotation: when you rotate a workspace's webhook secret, we continue to accept deliveries signed with the previous secret for up to 24 hours. If a signature check fails, first confirm which secret was active when the event was generated, then check whether a rotation happened inside the 24-hour window.

Test-mode events use the same signing scheme. The payload body includes `event_mode: "test"` so your handler can route them to a sandbox path.

We retry failed deliveries for up to 24 hours, so design handlers to be idempotent. We do not guarantee exactly-once delivery.

- Dropped "investigating possible signature drift" — that framing implies a product defect or incident, and Leo's evidence (plus our standard support practice) points at customer-side middleware parsing and reserializing the body before verification. There's no reason to expose our internal investigation posture in a customer reply.
- Reframed as "how signing works + the most common cause of this pattern," then 5 ordered checks (log raw body pre-parse, confirm framework isn't auto-parsing, replay byte-identical from our event log, bypass body-parsing middleware, check for charset/encoding rewraps). Closes with a low-friction ask for language + a redacted snippet if they want a closer look. No escalation language, no "we may have changed something," no incident framing.

Ready to send as-is. If you want a canonical webhook-signing doc link inline, point me at the URL and I'll drop it in.

---

Subject: Re: [their subject]

Hi [name],

Thanks for the detailed report — wanted to share a quick frame on how signatures work and the checks that usually clear this up.

Atlas webhook signatures are HMACs computed over the exact bytes of the request body as it arrives at your endpoint. Any transformation between receipt and verification — even invisible ones like JSON key reordering, whitespace normalization, or Unicode escaping — changes the bytes and breaks the match. This most often comes from middleware that parses the body into an object and reserializes it before the verifier sees it.

A few concrete checks, in order:

1. Log the raw request body immediately on receipt (before any parsing) and feed that exact byte sequence to the verifier. If mismatches disappear here, a transformation is happening upstream of verification.
2. If your framework auto-parses JSON bodies (e.g. express.json() in Node, request.body vs request.data in Django, Flask before_request hooks), confirm the verifier is reading the raw stream, not the parsed object.
3. Verify against a payload replayed byte-identically from our event log / dashboard. If the signature matches there but not in your environment, the drift is local.
4. Temporarily bypass body-parsing middleware and re-run the replay. If the mismatch clears, you've found it.
5. Confirm your HTTP server/client isn't applying charset normalization or content-encoding rewraps before the verifier reads the body.

If you can share the language/runtime and a small redacted snippet showing how the body reaches the verifier, I'll take a closer look. Happy to jump on a quick call if that's easier — just let me know a time.

Best,

arguments.title: Release decision — MER-1749 / MER-1823 (live-sync recovery UX)
arguments.body:
Internal decision note — Jake, Leo
Re: live-sync recovery edge reported on MER-1279

Decision
- Treat MER-1749 (reconcile patch so retry status refreshes correctly after timeout recovery without a page reload) and MER-1823 (stale timeout-banner cleanup so a successful retry clears the old timeout message in-session) as customer-impacting release work this week.
- Ship them in the small Wednesday or Thursday release only if Leo's last bounded timeout replay plus post-deploy smoke both come back clean.
- Hold the nice-to-have copy/UX cleanup items out of this release unless the branch is genuinely boring once 1749 and 1823 land.

Customer-impacting — IN this week's release
- MER-1749 — retry status refresh after timeout recovery, no reload required.
  - Why it belongs: the current behavior leaves the UI in a stale pending state long enough that the operator cannot tell whether the retry recovered. In the two workspaces support has seen this in (Evergreen Bank test workspace and one other current Mercury workspace on the same bounded live-sync path), support had to manually tell the account to refresh or re-open the page to see the recovered state. Three support touches off two accounts, same question each time. No duplicate sync jobs and no data-loss signal in the logs, but the first live-sync experience burns trust and generates repeat "did this actually run" traffic.
- MER-1823 — stale timeout-banner cleanup so a successful retry clears the old timeout message in the same session.
  - Why it belongs: old timeout messaging hangs around in-session after recovery, which compounds the stale pending state from 1749 and makes the recovery path look less reliable than it is.

Nice-to-have cleanup — OUT unless the branch is genuinely boring
- Retry helper-text cleanup.
- Timeout-banner copy polish.
- Minor pending-state wording cleanup that does not change behavior.
- Rationale for holding these: none of them reduce the support ambiguity that is actually driving the trust impact this week. If 1749 and 1823 are clean and the branch has no surprises, we can fold one or more of these into the same release; if anything is noisy, we drop them and keep the release small.

Scope boundaries (explicit)
- This is a recovery-UX fix, not a sync-engine or retry-policy change. No changes to when a retry fires, what counts as a source timeout, or how the bounded live-sync path behaves under failure — only what the user sees around a successful recovery.
- Frame the release notes accordingly: customer-visible improvement to recovery feedback, no change to retry semantics.

Gate before ship
- Leo's remaining bounded timeout replay comes back clean.
- Post-deploy smoke on the small release is clean.
- If either is noisy: ship 1749 + 1823 only if both still pass their own checks in isolation; otherwise hold the whole set to next week rather than rushing partial UX fixes.

Open question
- Confirm Wednesday vs Thursday target once Leo has a read on the replay timing.

Hey — before you post the Mercury support-polish fix in #eng-releases, here's the pre-green check (same shape you adopted after Leo's April review, so we're consistent).

Review steps required before posting
1. Leo's risk/evidence/readout sign-off
   - Short risk note: anything customer-visible that could read as a broader admin-state or permissions change? If yes, trim before posting.
   - Evidence: which surfaces touched, screenshots or short walkthrough from staging for each. The evidence has to make "this is a small polish" obvious at a glance.
   - Readout: 2–3 lines tying each release claim to its verification note. No claims without a matching note from Marcus.
2. Marcus's verification notes attached
   - Attach to the post (or link in-thread) the verification note(s) for each fix in the bundle. If a surface isn't covered, drop it from the release note rather than skipping the note.
3. Channel check
   - Posts in #eng-releases only — never #eng-all.
   - Frame as support polish, not an admin/permissions/perf/enterprise-readiness change.

Limits on the release claims
- Say only what shipped on the exact surfaces shown in staging proof.
- Do NOT imply any of the following, even as color:
  - a broader admin-state, admin-vs-billing-owner, or role-model change
  - new permissions, auth, or access behavior
  - enterprise-readiness work or a wider admin/billing cleanup
  - changes to retry/sync semantics or platform behavior under failure
  - future identity/admin-model commitments
- Support-polish wording stays narrow: copy/UI fix on a specific surface, tied to Marcus's verification note for that surface. If a claim doesn't have evidence, it doesn't go in.
- If the draft risks sounding bigger than the impl (like the invited-member handoff note Leo trimmed in April), pull it back to what the evidence actually supports.

Net: risk + evidence + readout, every claim tied to a verification note, channel is #eng-releases only. Ping me when Leo's signed off and I'll spot-check before it goes up.

tests.request: Email support@scaffold.dev a customer-ready explanation of API v2 webhook delivery behavior and how their integration should process incoming events.

input.query: Scaffold API v2 webhook delivery signature retry

input.body:
Hi,

Quick walkthrough of how API v2 webhook delivery works on our side and how your integration should process incoming events. This should cover what most teams need; reply on-thread if anything below doesn't match what you're seeing.

1. Delivery is at-least-once

We don't promise exactly-once delivery. If your endpoint doesn't acknowledge a delivery with a 2xx, our system retries the same payload — that includes 5xx responses (504 included), network errors, and request timeouts on our side. From your perspective this can look like duplicates, but they're the same event being re-attempted, not new emissions.

Practical implication: a single source event can hit your endpoint more than once. Design for that rather than against it.

2. event_id is the idempotency key

Every webhook payload carries a stable event_id that's unique per event. Your consumer should dedupe on event_id before processing — e.g., store it on first accept and short-circuit on subsequent matches. With that in place, retries from our side become invisible noise rather than duplicate work in your system.

If you're using a queue between your endpoint and the consumer, dedupe at the consumer (on the event_id from the payload), not just at the ingress, so retries that arrive out of order don't double-process.

3. Retries aren't a toggle you can disable

We get this question after any duplicate-event incident, so worth being direct: workspace-level "disable retries" isn't a setting we expose. Retries are load-bearing for at-least-once — turning them off would convert any temporary outage on your side into a missed event, which is a worse failure mode than the duplicate you're trying to avoid. If a particular event type is noisy in your environment, the right knob is your consumer's dedupe on event_id, not our retry behavior.

4. What we sign and how to verify it

Each request includes an X-Scaffold-Signature header (HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, keyed with the signing secret configured for your workspace) and an X-Scaffold-Timestamp header. Verify the signature against the raw request body before trusting the payload, and reject any request where the timestamp is more than ~5 minutes off the wall clock to limit replay window. Secrets are managed per workspace in your dashboard under Webhooks.

5. What to send us if something looks wrong

If you see behavior that doesn't fit the above — payloads with a missing or non-unique event_id, deliveries that continue well past our normal retry window, or events that arrive without a valid signature — send the event_ids and approximate UTC timestamps and we'll trace the delivery. For routine duplicates after a non-2xx on your side, no action needed; the consumer-side dedupe handles it.

Reference: docs.scaffold.dev/api-v2/webhooks covers the same points if you want to point your integration team at it.

Happy to jump on a quick call if it'd help your team align on the consumer-side handling.

Leo
Scaffold Support

# Compass Q3 read — internal closeout record

Date: 2026-07-16
Owner of record: Morgan
Status: Q3 hold holds. Compass stays internal — no customer-facing claim, GTM proof, staffing trigger, or Series C language from this read.

## Q3 reopen triggers (end-Q3, all 3 required — holding from 06-25/06-26)
1. ≥2 accounts outside Evergreen close Q3 renewals at GR ≥85%.
2. ≥1 Q3 renewal where Sarah/impl-only carries, no exec carry.
3. One retention number (NRR or GR), no caveats.

Inbound + Compass stay separate until triggers met.

## Final read — prompt hits (internal tally)
- Total retained prompt hits: 11
- Dated owner follow-up: 4
- Prompt-sightings only (no dated owner action): 7
- Customer-initiated: 0

### Dated owner follow-up (4)
1. Evergreen — Jul 2 admin-handoff. Sarah same-day current-state reply in thread; accepted; no advanced-admin promise made.
2. Evergreen — Jul 9/10 admin-handoff. Sarah current-flow wording; no product commitment.
3. Acme — Jul 9 export. Sarah → support; Leo first tech read; Jake bounded Atlas/API v2 sequencing; narrower replays done; no customer-visible data-loss signal. ### Prompt sightings only (7)
No dated owner action, no customer-initiated motion. Sourced from prompt-tool sightings across the quarter; not retell-able as Compass proof.

- Prompt sightings ≠ proof of Compass-driven retention or expansion.
- Acme export is Atlas/API v2 support work; not a Compass retention signal.
- Jake: no Compass-driven dashboard rebuild; no Atlas under Compass; no Mercury activation/admin scope from this read.
- Count of 11 retained hits is an internal tally — not a customer or investor metric.
- Zero customer-initiated Compass asks this quarter.

## What this means
- Hold holds: do not reopen Q3 Compass reframe until all 3 triggers land with end-Q3 evidence.
- Inbound customer renewals + Compass remain separate conversations.
- Owner-group (Sarah / Leo / Jake) gets the count + caveats in Discord; no spin, no reframe.
- Next review point: end-Q3 readout against the 3 triggers.

## Distribution
- Doc: this file.
- Deck: Q3 operating evidence slide updated with final count + hold.
- Channel: owner-group Discord post (count + caveats only).

# May 2026 board Q&A — overclaim guardrails

Working doc for Tuesday 05-26 board-packet prep. Five expected questions, short answer cores, guardrail framing. Not a polished memo.

---

## Q1 — Compass rollout

**Core:** Compass is useful internally at Evergreen and Acme only. No repeatability claim, no customer-facing claim, no GTM motion, no staffing implication, no fundraising read.

**Guardrail:** Internal-usefulness only. Do not frame as an automation wedge or repeatable playbook.

**Do not say:** "repeatable", "automation wedge", "next customer", "we can scale this internally out".

---

## Q2 — Mercury source-specific docs / support cleanup

**Core:** Support deflection and setup clarity. Mercury invite audit-label deployed 05-22; prod smoke pending.

**Guardrail:** Support-quality / hygiene work. Not activation lift, not retention proof, not a customer-facing win.

**Do not say:** "drove activation", "reduced churn", "customers adopting faster", "self-serve motion".

---

## Q3 — Evergreen April 214 MAD

**Core:** One standard $1,000 Growth overage. Standard MAD only, no offsets, CSV descriptive. Sarah (CS), Devon (Finance).

**Guardrail:** April overage accepted 05-08 as a note. Not expansion readiness. Not a custom admin commitment.

**Do not say:** "ready to expand", "precedent for custom admin tier", "Growth trajectory".

---

## Q4 — AWS + Pinecone

**Core:** Normal vendor hygiene. Pinecone remains monthly through Q2 (prepay declined 05-01). AWS is routine.

**Guardrail:** Vendor hygiene only. Not market-warming evidence. Not a procurement transformation.

**Do not say:** "market is heating", "we're locking in capacity", "vendor leverage is improving".

---

## Q5 — H1 posture

**Core:** Durability over motion. None of these reads reopen hiring, change GTM, or warm the market.

**Guardrail:** Reads close scope, they don't open it. April close = hygiene, not motion. Q3 is the real push; hiring tight until then.

**Do not say:** "we should revisit hiring", "GTM is accelerating", "window is opening", "ready to lean in".

---

## Open before packet freeze

- Mercury invite audit-label prod smoke — confirm landed before freeze. If slips, frame as "deployed, smoke pending", not "complete".
- Director Qs expected on Q1 and Q5 — keep both anchored to internal-usefulness only and durability-over-motion respectively.

- "We are treating this as internal-usefulness only and are not making a customer-facing or repeatability claim based on Q2."
- "Compass remains an internal operating tool. A customer-facing story would require a separate read and broader evidence."

tests.request: PR scaffold/mercury#5128 uses a broken-link icon for sync failure and a retry arrow as the persistent status icon. Post a review comment correcting the icon treatment and explaining why.

input.body:
Icon treatment in this PR mixes two semantically wrong glyphs with the sync status. A couple of notes before this lands:

1. Broken-link icon for sync failure — not appropriate here. The broken-link glyph reads as "dead/external resource" (404, broken URL, missing attachment). It tells the user "this thing doesn't exist," not "we couldn't talk to the server." Sync failure is a *transient operational* state on a resource the user knows exists, so it should use the same icon family as our other sync states (cloud-with-slash, or the red exclamation on the sync icon), not the link-broken glyph. Keeping failure in the sync family is what lets users pattern-match: same shape, different color/state.

2. Retry arrow as the persistent status icon — also wrong. A retry arrow is an *action affordance* ("click me to retry"), not a status. Rendering it persistently implies the icon itself is a button and trains users to tap it expecting an immediate retry — when in reality the sync worker may already be retrying on its own with backoff. Use the sync-in-progress / sync-failed glyph as the persistent state, and put the retry arrow only on the row action menu / a button that explicitly says "Retry."

Suggested swap for the persistent status row:
  - idle/synced: checkmark on cloud (existing)
  - syncing: rotating arrows on cloud (existing)
  - failed: red exclamation on cloud (replace broken-link)
  - retry: only as a row action, never as the persistent icon (replace persistent retry arrow)

Happy to send a follow-up patch if useful, but flagging now since this is the kind of thing that's painful to roll back once users start associating the broken-link glyph with "sync error" in support tickets.

messages.content:
1) Evergreen → repeatable

  Honest version: Evergreen is one account. Repeatable means a second independent win came from the same product mechanism, not from Evergreen-derived familiarity (and explicitly not Acme — that doesn't count).

  Evidence that actually moves it from "proof" to "playbook":
    - 2+ accounts in the same cohort with similar time-to-value, retention, expansion — driven by the same Scaffold mechanic, not bespoke services
    - Decomposition of "why Evergreen worked" into Scaffold-controlled factors vs. account-specific (industry, champion, internal readiness). If most of the win is account-specific, it's not repeatable
    - A documented motion with controllable inputs that a new AE/CSE can run without Evergreen context
    - At least one new win where the motion applied and Evergreen wasn't the reference account

  Until one of those lands, I keep saying "strong one-account proof" — not repeatable. Board story stays on retention + renewal evidence, not on Evergreen as a growth engine.

2) Compass staying alive

  Currently framed as narrowed learning — not launch, not behavior-change proof, not roadmap promise, not hiring trigger. If the only output is internal prompt work with no downstream artifact, it's a cost center wearing a research hat.

  Keep it alive only with all three:
    - Written learning objective naming the specific decision it informs (a Mercury feature, an Atlas capability, or a kill)
    - Kill criteria — what outcome, by when, means we stop
    - Named owner for the learning artifact, not just for the experiments

  If any of those is missing, wind it down. "We're learning things" is not a default justification.

3) Shaping the next financing story

  Not now. Q2 review window is no-Series-C-narrative by design. Jake owns the investor lane; gate is post-round, product updates only until then.

  Start shaping when all of these are true:
    - Retention + renewal evidence from this quarter is written up, not just felt
    - Mercury/Atlas has 2+ quarters of reliable-execution evidence
    - Compass either produced a roadmap input or was killed cleanly with a documented takeaway
    - I can answer "what changed in the last 6-9 months that supports a bigger round" with concrete artifacts, not aspirations
    - Evergreen is either repeatable (Q1 bar met) or honestly de-positioned from the growth story

  Earliest realistic window: Q3 push, after the board story is solid. Until then, any later-stage investor who asks about Evergreen/Mercury gets routed to Jake with the current-quarter frame — no fresh narrative.

[2024-03-22T09:06:00-07:00] HR’s finalist packet for Nadia is here.

From: HR
To: Morgan Chen, Devon Hayes
Cc: Sarah Kim
Date: Fri, Mar 22, 2024 8:41 AM PT
Subject: Nadia Singh finalist packet + proposed final loop

Morgan / Devon / Sarah —

Per the search calibration, sending the finalist packet for Nadia Singh inline below. She is the strongest fit we have seen for the actual brief: taking messy design-partner and early enterprise-adoption learning and turning it into a repeatable customer-growth motion, without treating roadmap exceptions as the job.

This is not a generic enterprise-sales VP readout. I’ve kept the interview notes in the same comparison frame we agreed to use for early calls, then pulled out reference themes and the proposed final topics that seem most worth probing.

-----------------------------------
CANDIDATE SNAPSHOT
-----------------------------------
Name: Nadia Singh
Current lane: customer-growth / enterprise-adoption leadership at growth-stage infrastructure/product companies
Relevant pattern match:
- has built post-design-partner onboarding and expansion motions before there was a mature sales org
- is comfortable with technical buyers, implementation friction, and early product gaps
- repeatedly frames customer trust as “clear boundaries + good follow-through,” not promise-making
- strongest when the company has signal but not yet a system

Why she rose to the top of the slate:
- Other strong candidates tended to drift into classic enterprise-sales language quickly (territory coverage, comp plans, pipeline mechanics, “what can product commit by quarter-end”). Nadia stayed anchored on activation evidence, adoption risk, expansion blockers, and operating handoffs.
- She appears genuinely comfortable in the in-between stage Scaffold is actually in: enough pull to matter, not enough structure to hide behind.

-----------------------------------
INTERVIEW NOTES
-----------------------------------

1) HR calibration screen
Date: Mar 11
Format: 45 min

Repeatable enterprise adoption
- Strongest section of the call.
- Nadia described her best work as turning “founder memory and scattered customer anecdotes” into a small set of repeatable stages, owner handoffs, and leading indicators.
- She asked early what design-partner learning currently lives in people’s heads vs. docs vs. product telemetry.
- She did not assume a big CS function, implementation team, or formal sales engineering layer already exists.

Judgment about not promising product
- Good boundary instinct.
- Said directly that early customer-growth leaders can do real damage if they confuse “earning trust” with “manufacturing certainty.”
- Her framing: if a feature is not committed internally, the external language has to stay at the level of current constraint, current workaround, and what evidence would change prioritization.
- She differentiated packaging/clarity work from true roadmap commitments without being evasive.

Ability to work without a mature sales org
- Comfortable with ambiguity and founder-heavy environments.
- She expects to draft playbooks herself at the beginning.
- Explicitly said she does not need a full RevOps stack to start; wants a reliable source of customer notes, activation milestones, and clear owner routing.
- Watchout: she has usually had at least one operations or program partner by the time the motion starts scaling.

Technical-buyer comfort
- High.
- Spoke fluently about technical evaluators, security/procurement drag, admin setup confusion, and where implementation friction masks as “customer hesitancy.”
- Did not oversell herself as a product manager, but seems able to hold her own with product and engineering leads.

Stage fit
- Good fit for the role as currently calibrated.
- She understands the difference between helping the company learn from enterprise-like customers and prematurely pretending the company is already a fully tooled enterprise vendor.
- Motivated by building the operating system, not inhe…

3 conversations instead of HR's 5. Same coverage on all four asks. ~2.5 hrs panel time + 45 min same-day debrief. One shared scenario spine across all 3 so answers stay comparable.

  MERCURY ACTIVATION              Conv 1
  EVERGREEN-STYLE SIGNALS         Conv 2
  EXPANSION FAILURE MODES         Conv 3
  HANDOFFS WITH SARAH + DEVON     Conv 2 (primary) + Conv 1 (implicit)
  BESPOKE PROMISES / VP SALES     out-of-bounds in all 3


======
STRUCTURE
======
  Conv 1 — Operating shape           60 min   Morgan + Devon
  Conv 2 — Customer thread + handoffs 60 min   Sarah + Devon
  Conv 3 — Expansion diagnosis        45 min   Morgan
  Debrief  — same day                 45 min   all interviewers + HR


======
SHARED SCENARIO SPINE
======
Hand to every interviewer the morning of. Use the same one in all three conversations.

  - Stage: Mercury. Post-design-partner signal, a small set of
    enterprise-leaning accounts, no mature sales org.
  - Inputs: scattered activation notes, admin/security/procurement
    asks, expansion softness in 2-3 accounts, founder context split
    across Sarah and Devon.
  - Constraints: no shipping dates to share; SSO / posture /
    procurement-packet work is in progress but not releasable as
    commitments; bespoke roadmap promises are off the table.
  - Owner split: Sarah = customer-thread continuity. Devon = commercial
    / procurement framing. Product = product truth. Candidate = the
    customer-growth motion.
  - Goal: turn messy evidence into a repeatable motion without
    inventing structure the company doesn't have yet.


======
DEBRIEF SCORING (4 dimensions, 1-5 each, all interviewers)
======
  1. Evidence discipline   — asks for minimum viable inputs, no theater
  2. Boundary judgment     — separates packaging from product truth,
                             no bespoke promises
  3. Owner mapping         — names when she'd pull Sarah / Devon /
                             product; doesn't absorb everything
                             customer-ish
  4. Stage realism         — sequences over completeness; opts into
                             mess with clear eyes


======
CONV 1 — OPERATING SHAPE  (Morgan + Devon, 60 min)
======
Covers: 30/60/90 + stage fit + what she would NOT build in Q1.

  SETUP (3 min)
    Read the scenario spine aloud. Hand her the shared scenario sheet.

  PROMPT 1 — 30/60/90 (20 min)
    Day one. Mercury has meaningful design-partner signal, a small set
    of enterprise-leaning accounts, activation evidence scattered across
    people and notes, and the team is still founder-led in several
    important places. Sketch the first 30, 60, 90 days. What do you do
    in week one? What do you defer?

  PROMPT 2 — Minimum viable evidence set (15 min)
    What is the minimum set of customer evidence you'd need before
    you'd call any part of this motion repeatable? What inputs would
    you refuse to build a process on top of?

  PROMPT 3 — What you would NOT build in Q1 (10 min)
    What's the most common thing a customer-growth leader is tempted
    to build in quarter one that you would actively resist? Why?

  WHAT TO LISTEN FOR
    - Asks for sources of customer notes before talking dashboards
    - Distinguishes activation friction from broader expansion /
      commercial issues
    - Names an explicit cadence for synthesis and owner routing
    - Sequences over completeness; no hiring or territory design in
      week one
    - Treats customer-growth as one of several owners, not the
      customer-ish catchall
    - Reads the constraint set as the brief, not a problem to
      negotiate around


======
CONV 2 — CUSTOMER THREAD + HANDOFFS  (Sarah + Devon, 60 min)
======
Covers: Evergreen-style enterprise-readiness pressure + owner split
with Sarah and Devon. Sarah leads; Devon is in the room specifically
because commercial-framing ownership needs to be discussed live.

  SETUP (3 min)
    Same scenario spine. Add: the current shape of enterprise-
    readiness …

arguments.title: People-Ops Runbook — Hard Policies
arguments.body:
# People-Ops Runbook — Hard Policies

This document captures hard rules for hiring, onboarding, and people operations.
Hard rules are non-negotiable and have no exceptions unless explicitly overridden
in writing by the CEO.

---

## H1. Background verification for principal-and-up leadership hires

**Effective:** 2023-05-01
**Owner:** Recruiter Ops
**Scope:** All candidates at the Principal level and above (Principal, Staff,
Principal Staff, Director, VP, C-level, and equivalent leadership tracks).

**Rule:** Every candidate at Principal level or above MUST complete third-party
background verification before any offer letter is finalized. No exceptions on
leadership hires.

**Trigger:** Automated — kicks off when a candidate is moved to the "Principal+"
stage in the ATS workflow. Not ad hoc; recruiter ops does not initiate or skip
this step manually.

**Workflow owner:** Recruiter Ops owns end-to-end execution, including vendor
coordination, result review, and gating the offer-letter step in the ATS until
verification clears.

**Enforcement:** The offer-letter approval step in the ATS is gated on a
"verification cleared" flag. Offer letters cannot be sent for principal-and-up
candidates until that flag is set.

**Exceptions:** None. Any exception requires explicit written approval from the
CEO and is logged in the candidate's ATS record with rationale.

---

*Maintained by People Ops. Add new hard rules below this line using the same
H-numbered format.*

# Operations director reference checks

**Purpose:** Brief reference for HR going into the next ops-director search.
Captures what we missed when we hired Reece (late 2021) and what to verify
this round so we don't burn three weeks of board time on someone else's
unfinished exit.

**Author:** Morgan Chen
**Date:** 2026-09-14
**Audience:** HR (lead), Morgan, Devon

---

## What we missed on Reece

- **Prior exit terms were not surfaced by any reference.** Two months in,
  we learned he'd been quietly pushed out of his last role under terms no
  reference had volunteered. Nobody on the loop told us why the last
  chapter had ended.
- **References were positive, recent, and on-narrative — and therefore
  useless on the actual risk.** The signal we needed (why the previous
  role ended, under what terms, and what the employer would say off-record)
  was not in the packet.
- **Cost:** ~3 weeks of board time once it surfaced, with no operating
  output. The disruption was entirely about unwinding someone else's
  unfinished business, not about anything we learned after hire.

## What HR should verify this time

Treat these as **required** checks for the ops-director finalist. Same
reference-quality bar as a Director+ hire per the People-Ops Runbook
(background verification is already ATS-gated; the items below are the
reference layer on top).

1. **Prior exit terms, in writing.**
   - For each of the last two roles, get a reference who can speak to
     why the role ended (resignation, mutual, termination, push-out,
     restructuring).
   - If the answer is anything other than a clean resignation, ask the
     employer reference directly: were there severance terms, an NDA, a
     non-disparagement clause, or any ongoing dispute?
   - Ask the candidate the same question, in the finalist loop, before
     references are contacted. Compare answers; flag any divergence.

2. **Off-record read from a peer or cross-functional partner.**
   - One reference must be a peer/partner at the prior company, not the
     hiring manager. Managers optimize for narrative; peers surface the
     day-to-day behavior that drives ops friction.

3. **Reason for leaving each prior role, named directly.**
   - Do not accept "time for a new challenge" or "cultural mismatch" as
     the final answer. Push once for specifics; if the reference won't
     answer, that itself is a signal.

4. **Tenure-and-exit pattern check.**
   - List every role in the last 10 years with start/end dates and stated
     reason for leaving. Look for short tenures clustered around exits
     that aren't clean resignations. Surface the pattern in the packet;
     don't make Morgan or Devon reconstruct it.

5. **What the candidate would say went wrong.**
   - Ask the finalist directly: what's something you shipped that didn't
     land, and what was your role in it? Compare to the reference read.
     Ops directors in particular need to own failure publicly; inability
     to name one is a flag.

6. **Board-time cost framing in the packet.**
   - The finalist packet must include a one-paragraph "things we'd learn
     too late if we don't check now" section, so we don't repeat the
     Reece pattern of finding out the real story two months in.

## Process notes

- References are contacted after the finalist loop, not before, so the
  candidate has already committed to a reason-for-leaving story we can
  pressure-test against the references.
- If any reference declines to comment on exit terms, HR pauses the loop
  and escalates to Morgan before proceeding. Silence on this point is
  itself a finding.
- Keep the packet short. The goal is for the references to surface what
  we'd otherwise learn the hard way — not for HR to write a memo.

---

Related: People-Ops Runbook — Hard Policies (H1, background verification
for Principal+ hires, ATS-gated). This document is the reference-layer
companion for the ops-director search specifically.

arguments.title: Compass — first Q3 read (prep doc)
arguments.body:
# Compass — first Q3 read (prep doc)

First-pass prep. Owner: Morgan. Status: working draft, not a board-facing artifact.

## 0. Frame

Compass v0.1 is still discovery. The Q3 read is owner-routed evidence, not a
broader-exposure claim. The one question for the room is the same as April:
**did account-team behavior change, or is this cleaner internal follow-up?**

Sightings alone do not count. A row is only usable when it has a dated owner
follow-up attached.

## 1. Row schema (what Anna and Sarah are returning against)

One row per prompt sighting. Fields:

1. account
2. prompt type — renewal-risk / admin-friction OR post-first-live-sync expansion
3. prompt sighting date
4. owner who saw it
5. evidence source link or account-thread excerpt
6. caveat
7. owner follow-up date, if any
8. outcome or current status

If a row is missing a dated owner follow-up, it does not move into the read.

## 2. Guardrails (hard)

- No customer-facing claims from this read.
- No GTM proof implied.
- No staffing trigger.
- Acme export row stays Atlas / API v2 support context — not Compass proof.
- Evergreen admin-handoff row is useful only with Sarah's dated current-state
  follow-up attached.
- Linear "green" ≠ proof — Honeycomb evidence required for any launch-readiness
  ticket cited.

## 3. Boundaries held

- Acme thread stays Compass-free. No Compass screenshots / Mercury packet flow
  to Acme via Compass.
- Devon stays out of the Compass read lane.
- Inbound (Sofia / investor-warming) and Compass stay separate channels.

## 4. Decision boundaries for the read

In scope only:

- Continue / pause / tighten owner-group use of Compass.
- Continue / drop a specific prompt type based on the dated rows.
- Tighten or relax any per-account boundary above.

Out of scope (gated to the May / next board cycle, not this read):

- Customer-facing proof of behavior change.
- Board-dashboard framing.
- Hiring implication.

If the room drifts there, defer in writing.

## 5. Owners

- Anna — definitions lock + terminology in the room.
- Sarah — Evergreen current-state rows (annual-account only); Acme live signals
  owner, with Greg / Nadia / Jake.
- Leo — source-recency caveat sentence.
- Jake — prompt-level implementation status (no dashboard rebuild implied).
- Nadia — behavior-change-or-cleaner-follow-up read for the room.
- Morgan — boundary enforcement, decision-deferrals.

## 6. What the room may leave with

(A) Continue current scope, named owners, next-check date.
(B) Continue with named tightening (narrower date window, dropped prompt type,
added caveat) and named owner for the change.

Not on the table: broader-exposure decision, customer-facing claim,
