[2023-05-17T09:31:00-07:00] Anna’s v0.4 retention package landed:

From: Anna Martinez
To: Morgan Chen; Devon Hayes
Date: 2023-05-17 09:11 PT
Subject: Retention package v0.4 — weekly operating cuts + quarterly board view

Pulled off warehouse snapshots through 2023-05-16 23:10 PT. This is the first version I’d actually use operationally. I stopped trying to make one chart do both jobs.

Recommendation
1) Mercury weekly gets signup-week operating cuts with control bands.
2) The board gets quarterly first-paid cohorts only.
3) Keep the event-mapping caveats attached to the weekly package, not the board slide.

Definitions used in both views
- Cohort anchor: first paid workspace date. For self-serve workspaces that convert later, the cohort starts at first paid date, not initial signup.
- Activated by D14: workspace recorded 3+ core product actions across 2+ active users by day 14.
- Retained at W6: workspace recorded at least 1 core action in week 6.
- Expansion-ready by D45: billed usage or seat growth crossed the threshold that historically precedes an expansion conversation; I used invoice-backed billed delta, not the plan-change event.
- Admin friction flag: setup or permissions issue tied to owner/admin actions in the first 14 days.
- Control band: Wilson interval on the cohort proportion. Point estimate alone is too twitchy at this sample size.

Mercury operating view — weekly cohorts, internal only

Matured cohorts (safe for D14 + W6 read)

| First paid week | n workspaces | D14 activated | W6 retained | D45 expansion-ready | Admin friction flags / acct | Read |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| 2023-03-06 | 27 | 56% [37-73] | 44% [28-63] | 15% [6-33] | 0.48 | baseline after March cleanup started |
| 2023-03-13 | 29 | 59% [41-75] | 47% [30-65] | 17% [8-34] | 0.41 | basically same week, slightly cleaner setup path |
| 2023-03-20 | 31 | 61% [43-76] | 49% [32-67] | 19% [10-35] | 0.38 | activation lift might be real; retention still within overlap |
| 2023-03-27 | 28 | 64% [46-79] | 50% [32-68] | 21% [10-40] | 0.35 | admin pain down again; good sign, still not definitive |
| 2023-04-03 | 30 | 63% [45-78] | 52% [34-69] | 23% [12-40] | 0.29 | best clean operating week in this run |

Fresh but incomplete cohorts (D14 only; do not talk about retention yet)

| First paid week | n workspaces | D14 activated | Admin setup complete by D10 | Admin friction flags / acct | Read |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| 2023-04-10 | 26 | 62% [42-79] | 54% [35-72] | 0.31 | still consistent with improvement, not special |
| 2023-04-17 | 24 | 65% [44-81] | 58% [37-77] | 0.27 | best early admin signal so far |
| 2023-04-24 | 27 | 63% [44-79] | 56% [37-73] | 0.30 | flat to slightly better |

Short read on the weekly package
- Activation and admin setup are moving in the right direction from late March onward.
- W6 retention is improving a little, but the week-to-week moves are still inside overlapping bands.
- The cleanest operating signal right now is reduced admin friction, not a dramatic retention jump.
- This is useful for weekly decisions on activation, expansion follow-up, and admin pain. It is not a board chart.

Board view — quarterly cohorts, safe enough to defend

| First paid quarter | start accounts | M3 logo retention | M6 logo retention | M12 logo retention | Net revenue retention at latest mature point | Notes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| 2022 Q1 | 21 | 86% | 81% | 71% | 108% @ M12 | raw is 121% if the oversized early expansion customer stays untrimmed; I would not headline the raw number |
| 2022 Q2 | 24 | 88% | 82% | 74% | 110% @ M12 | first cohort with the cleaner onboarding path reflected consistently |
| 2022 Q3 | 29 | 89% | 84% | — | 113% @ M9 | okay to show curve through current maturity; not enough age for M12 claim |
| 2022 Q4 | 32 | 91% | 85% | — | 116% @ M6 | reads as flattening after onboarding improvements; too early to overclaim durability |
| 2023 Q1 | 35 | 90% | — | — | 118…

MERCURY WEEKLY (Jake owns, you + Devon review — product/operating only, no investor routing):

- D14 activation by signup week with bands, plus admin setup completion line and admin friction flags/acct. This is where the signal is clearest week to week.
- D45 expansion-ready, but only as a directional operating read. Invoice-backed billed delta stays the source of truth; ignore `plan_upgraded`.
- W6 retention is for the matured cohorts only (3/6 → 4/3). For 4/10 onward, keep partial rows visually separated and don't put a number on the retention cell.
- n in the first column of every table. Band shading on the operating chart itself.
- Caption on the chart, verbatim from Anna: "weekly cohorts; internal operating signal only; treat only sustained or out-of-band movement as signal."

BOARD VIEW (separate stream — DO NOT route to Jake):

- Quarterly first-paid cohorts only. No weekly cuts on a board slide, period.
- Headline NRR is the trimmed read. Raw 121% (2022 Q1) lives in the sensitivity footnote, not in the headline number.
- 2023 Q1 row stays labeled immature — no M6/M12 claims drawn off it. Same for Q4 if anyone asks for M12.
- One footnote on the main chart, full stop: "Quarterly first-paid cohorts; latest quarter shown only through available maturity; top-1 expansion outlier trimmed in companion sensitivity view."
- No control bands on the board chart. Bands stay attached to the Mercury operating chart only — that's where the noise gets handled.

WHERE CAVEATS BELONG (so weekly wiggle can't leak into the board chart):

- Event-mapping note (`plan_upgraded` retries, invoice-backed expansion) → Mercury operating chart. Not board.
- `workspace_activated` redefinition + 3/14 backcast → methodology footnote on Mercury package only.
- 2023-04-04 to 04-07 admin invite backfill gap → Mercury operating note; doesn't touch the board retention curve at all.
- Self-serve reactivation 21-day rule → methodology footnote on Mercury only. If anyone wonders why weekly isn't 2-3 points prettier, the answer is here, not on the board.

GATING v1 (Anna's own open items — don't ship until these close):

- Finish the 04-04 to 04-07 admin invite backfill check.
- Verify the two April workspaces with invoice deltas but no matching seat-change logs. If those are real expansion without seat logs, the D45 number is overstating.
- Lock one owner for the warehouse pull. Side sheets are how definitions drift between Mercury and the board — that's the failure mode this whole split exists to prevent.

Bottom line: Mercury gets the weekly cuts + admin friction + bands + event-mapping caveats, board gets the quarterly trimmed view + one footnote. If anyone later asks for "the weekly number" on a board slide, the answer stays no.

[2023-05-17T09:31:00-07:00] Anna’s v0.4 retention package landed:

Subject: Retention package v0.4 — weekly operating cuts + quarterly board view

Pulled off warehouse snapshots through 2023-05-16 23:10 PT. This is the first version I’d actually use operationally. I stopped trying to make one chart do both jobs.

Recommendation
1) Mercury weekly gets signup-week operating cuts with control bands.
2) The board gets quarterly first-paid cohorts only.
3) Keep the event-mapping caveats attached to the weekly package, not the board slide.

Definitions used in both views
- Cohort anchor: first paid workspace date. For self-serve workspaces that convert later, the cohort starts at first paid date, not initial signup.
- Activated by D14: workspace recorded 3+ core product actions across 2+ active users by day 14.
- Retained at W6: workspace recorded at least 1 core action in week 6.
- Expansion-ready by D45: billed usage or seat growth crossed the threshold that historically precedes an expansion conversation; I used invoice-backed billed delta, not the plan-change event.
- Admin friction flag: setup or permissions issue tied to owner/admin actions in the first 14 days.
- Control band: Wilson interval on the cohort proportion. Point estimate alone is too twitchy at this sample size.

Mercury operating view — weekly cohorts, internal only

Matured cohorts (safe for D14 + W6 read)

| First paid week | n workspaces | D14 activated | W6 retained | D45 expansion-ready | Admin friction flags / acct | Read |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- |

| First paid week | n workspaces | D14 activated | Admin setup complete by D10 | Admin friction flags / acct | Read |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| 2023-04-10 | 26 | 62% [42-79] | 54% [35-72] | 0.31 | still consistent with improvement, not special |
| 2023-04-17 | 24 | 65% [44-81] | 58% [37-77] | 0.27 | best early admin signal so far |
| 2023-04-24 | 27 | 63% [44-79] | 56% [37-73] | 0.30 | flat to slightly better |

Short read on the weekly package
- Activation and admin setup are moving in the right direction from late March onward.
- W6 retention is improving a little, but the week-to-week moves are still inside overlapping bands.
- The cleanest operating signal right now is reduced admin friction, not a dramatic retention jump.
- This is useful for weekly decisions on activation, expansion follow-up, and admin pain. It is not a board chart.

Board view — quarterly cohorts, safe enough to defend

| First paid quarter | start accounts | M3 logo retention | M6 logo retention | M12 logo retention | Net revenue retention at latest mature point | Notes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| 2022 Q1 | 21 | 86% | 81% | 71% | 108% @ M12 | raw is 121% if the oversized early expansion customer stays untrimmed; I would not headline the raw number |
| 2022 Q2 | 24 | 88% | 82% | 74% | 110% @ M12 | first cohort with the cleaner onboarding path reflected consistently |
| 2022 Q3 | 29 | 89% | 84% | — | 113% @ M9 | okay to show curve through current maturity; not enough age for M12 claim |
| 2022 Q4 | 32 | 91% | 85% | — | 116% @ M6 | reads as flattening after onboarding improvements; too early to overclaim durability |
| 2023 Q1 | 35 | 90% | — | — | 118…

MERCURY WEEKLY (Jake owns, you + Devon review — product/operating only, no investor routing):

- D14 activation by signup week with bands, plus admin setup completion line and admin friction flags/acct. This is where the signal is clearest week to week.
- D45 expansion-ready, but only as a directional operating read. Invoice-backed billed delta stays the source of truth; ignore `plan_upgraded`.
- W6 retention is for the matured cohorts only (3/6 → 4/3). For 4/10 onward, keep partial rows visually separated and don't put a number on the retention cell.
- n in the first column of every table. Band shading on the operating chart itself.
- Caption on the chart, verbatim from Anna: "weekly cohorts; internal operating signal only; treat only sustained or out-of-band movement as signal."

BOARD VIEW (separate stream — DO NOT route to Jake):

- Quarterly first-paid cohorts only. No weekly cuts on a board slide, period.
- Headline NRR is the trimmed read. Raw 121% (2022 Q1) lives in the sensitivity footnote, not in the headline number.
- 2023 Q1 row stays labeled immature — no M6/M12 claims drawn off it. Same for Q4 if anyone asks for M12.
- One footnote on the main chart, full stop: "Quarterly first-paid cohorts; latest quarter shown only through available maturity; top-1 expansion outlier trimmed in companion sensitivity view."
- No control bands on the board chart. Bands stay attached to the Mercury operating chart only — that's where the noise gets handled.

WHERE CAVEATS BELONG (so weekly wiggle can't leak into the board chart):

- Event-mapping note (`plan_upgraded` retries, invoice-backed expansion) → Mercury operating chart. Not board.
- `workspace_activated` redefinition + 3/14 backcast → methodology footnote on Mercury package only.
- 2023-04-04 to 04-07 admin invite backfill gap → Mercury operating note; doesn't touch the board retention curve at all.
- Self-serve reactivation 21-day rule → methodology footnote on Mercury only. If anyone wonders why weekly isn't 2-3 points prettier, the answer is here, not on the board.

GATING v1 (Anna's own open items — don't ship until these close):

- Finish the 04-04 to 04-07 admin invite backfill check.
- Verify the two April workspaces with invoice deltas but no matching seat-change logs. If those are real expansion without seat logs, the D45 number is overstating.
- Lock one owner for the warehouse pull. Side sheets are how definitions drift between Mercury and the board — that's the failure mode this whole split exists to prevent.

Bottom line: Mercury gets the weekly cuts + admin friction + bands + event-mapping caveats, board gets the quarterly trimmed view + one footnote. If anyone later asks for "the weekly number" on a board slide, the answer stays no.

This note stays on the existing September / October 2023 external Mercury cohort package. It does not introduce a broader pipeline view, weekly operating cuts, or sample-preview diagnostics.

For the September and October 2023 external cohorts, 'entered the bounded Mercury flow' means an account entered the current bounded Mercury setup path used in the external package: invited into the product, able to access by the current invite / magic-link path, able to interact with preview-only sample data if present, and then progress toward connecting a real source and completing a first live sync. 2) Activation definition
For the outside-reader view, activated within 7 days means that within the first seven days after entering the bounded Mercury flow, the account either:
- connected a real source, or
- completed a first live sync.

The following do not count as activation:
- sample import / preview-only behavior
- invite sent

In the October 2023 cohort, 19 of 27 accounts were activated within 7 days and 16 of 27 completed first live sync within 7 days. The full gap between those two numbers is 3 accounts that connected a real source within 7 days but did not complete first live sync in that same seven-day window.

There is no additional preview-only, invite-only, or source-selected-only state inside the activation numerator.

4) Expansion / longer-window caveat
The external package stays week-one focused because that is the defensible read from the current September / October cohort set. tests.request: Create and save a short methodology document explaining the October 2023 Mercury cohort's seven-day activation and first-live-sync counts, including the figures and why they differ.

input.body:
Mercury October 2023 cohort — 7-day activation vs first-live-sync methodology
Internal methodology note. Scope: bounded Mercury flow only. Window: week one only.

Cohort figures (October 2023, bounded Mercury flow)
- Accounts entering bounded flow: 27
- Activated within 7 days: 19/27 (70%)
- Reached first live sync within 7 days: 16/27 (59%)
- Gap: 3 accounts

Activation definition (outside-reader)
- Activated = account hit real_source_connected OR first_live_sync_completed within 7 days of workspace creation.
- Excluded from activation numerator: sample_import_completed by itself; preview/sample-only behavior.
- Supporting only, not activation: invite_sent, invite accepted, preview viewed, source selected in-product.

Why activation and first-live-sync differ (the 3-account gap)
- In October, the 3-account gap is the full difference between 19 activated and 16 first live sync in the same seven-day window.
- Those 3 accounts reached real_source_connected within 7 days but did not reach first_live_sync_completed within the same 7-day window.
- No preview-only, invite-only, or sample-only bucket is inside the activation numerator; those categories are explicitly excluded.
- The gap is real, bounded, and the same construction holds in September (15 activated = 12 first live sync + 3 connected without first live sync in window).

Week-one activation split (transparent, not a new external metric)

| Cohort | Accounts entering bounded flow | First live sync within 7 days | Real source connected within 7 days, no first live sync in same window | Activated within 7 days |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Oct 2023 | 27 | 16/27 (59%) | 3/27 | 19/27 (70%) |

Reading notes
- Activation lift = more accounts clearing real-source connection and week-one live sync, not preview/sample behavior.
- The split is shown to make the activated vs first-live-sync difference transparent; it is not a new external sub-metric.
- Window is week one only. Late-October cohorts do not support a clean longer-window expansion read.
- Expansion after the initial admin / setup path is not part of this note and remains uneven.

messages.content:
[2024-10-18T10:24:00-07:00] Can you review HR’s October all-hands run-of-show and suggest tighter edits for my opener? I’m mostly worried the “enterprise push” wording makes the company focus sound broader than it is. Keep the language tied to current shipped facts and Q4 boundaries, not a bigger enterprise story.

October All-Hands — HR Draft Run of Show
Draft status: sent for Morgan review
Prepared by: HR
Audience: full company

Purpose
- Keep the company update short and factual.
- Reinforce Q4 focus and current decision boundaries.
- Use pre-collected questions only; no open-mic segment.
- Keep product and commercial language aligned with what has actually shipped.

Working theme
- What is more real now, what remains intentionally bounded, and what we are watching in Q4.

Meeting shape
- Total planned length: 34 minutes
- Format: short company update + pre-collected questions
- Live answers only on approved current topics
- Remaining questions routed async or to named owners after the meeting

Run of show

0:00–0:01
Owner: HR
Slide: title slide
Notes:
- Welcome everyone.
- Quick reminder that the meeting is recorded for teammates who cannot attend live.
- Hand off directly to Morgan.

0:01–0:07
Owner: Morgan Chen
Slide: Where we are now
Segment: six-minute opener
Speaker draft:

Thanks, everyone. I want to keep this one pretty direct.

A lot of the work we have been doing over the last few months is now showing up in a way that is more concrete and easier to talk about honestly. That is good for us internally, and it is good for the company because it lets us operate off evidence instead of momentum theater.

First, on product and release reality: we shipped the first Mercury enterprise-readiness slice into production for scoped enterprise accounts. The shipped pieces are specific: SAML SSO, admin-side audit-history events for invite, source, and admin changes, and clearer separation between admin and billing-owner responsibilities. That matters because those were real gaps for a set of larger customers, and now they are real capabilities we can point to without stretching the story.

Second, on platform and customer trust: Atlas support and release handling are on a steadier path. Customer-facing Atlas issues now route through the support rotation, Leo takes the first technical read, and Jake continues to own product priority and sequencing. That split is not glamorous, but it is important. It means customer issues are getting a cleaner technical read, product tradeoffs are staying with the right owner, and we are not pretending a process gap is solved by everyone swarming it.

Third, on the market side: our enterprise push is producing better conversations, but I want to be careful about what that does and does not mean. It means larger accounts are taking Scaffold more seriously when they look at setup, admin expectations, and reliability questions. It does not mean we suddenly have a broad enterprise machine, and it does not mean every larger-customer request should bend roadmap gravity.

That distinction matters a lot right now. The board discussion last month was constructive precisely because the facts are more real now, not because we told a bigger story. The line remains the same: more room, same discipline. Defensible story, not a bigger story.

So for Q4, our watchlist is still the same three things. One is Evergreen paid-pilot adoption. Two is renewal and expansion evidence. Three is Nadia’s account-source quality: are the stronger enterprise conversations coming from a repeatable lane, or are they still too dependent on one-off situations and bespoke pull. Those are the signals that matter. They are the board-facing signals, and they are the right internal signals too.

That also means some things are intentionally not changing yet. We are not building a broad field-sales motion right now. We are not opening a separate RevOps or CS lane right now. We are not reopening a second Mercury engineering req right now…

The worry is right. "Enterprise push" frames it as a coordinated outbound motion; what's actually happening is stronger inbound from a handful of larger accounts under the Q4 GTM freeze. A few surgical edits:

PRIMARY EDIT
- Replace "our enterprise push is producing better conversations" with "larger-account pull is producing more substantive conversations"
- "Pull" reads as demand-side (opposite of push); "larger-account" stays specific and avoids promoting "enterprise" from a customer segment to a motion

SECONDARY (same paragraph)
- Drop "suddenly" — softens the claim without adding meaning
- Swap "broad enterprise machine" → "broad enterprise motion" so the guardrail language matches the Q4 freeze phrasing you already use ("no broad field-sales build," "no separate RevOps or CS lane")

CLEAN REWRITE OF THE PARAGRAPH
Third, on the market side: larger-account pull is producing more substantive conversations, but I want to be careful about what that does and does not mean. It means larger accounts are taking Scaffold more seriously on setup, admin expectations, and reliability. It does not mean we have a broad enterprise motion, and it does not mean every larger-customer request should bend roadmap gravity.

WHAT I LEFT ALONE
- "First Mercury enterprise-readiness slice into production for scoped enterprise accounts" — "first" + "slice" + "scoped" keep it tight; matches shipped scope (SAML SSO, admin-audit for invite/source/admin, admin vs billing-owner split)
- "More room, same discipline. Defensible story, not a bigger story." — doing exactly the work you want
- The three-item watchlist (Evergreen paid-pilot adoption, renewal/expansion evidence, Nadia's account-source quality) — locked to board lens, keep
- The "not changing yet" trio (no field-sales build, no RevOps/CS lane, no second Mercury eng req) — guardrail intact, keep
- "Not a blank check to describe the product as fully enterprise-ready" — keep
- Closer ("building from proof instead of wishful extrapolation") — keep

ONE THING TO CONSIDER
- The opener is 6 minutes, which is long for an opener on a 34-min meeting. The middle (Atlas/support split and Q4 watchlist) carries weight, but the bullet stack at the end ("setup clarity, sync trust, release discipline…") mostly repeats points Jake, Leo, and Devon will hit. Could compress by ~60–90 seconds without losing signal. Want me to draft a tighter version, or stop at wording?

He started panting, turned back early, and came home after only a short stretch. He ate normally afterward and has no vomiting, leg favoring, or refusal of flat ground. Jamie and I talked it through and we are treating this as heat timing, not an emergency or a new vet issue. For the rest of the warm season, the walker instructions need to be stricter: on hot days he should be walked before 10:30 AM; if that cool window is missed, the walk should be skipped rather than made up at midday; and when he starts stiff, walks should stay short and flat.

arguments.title: Compass v0.1 — Tuesday signal-routing working session
arguments.body:
Date: Tue 1-21  ·  60 min  ·  Anna, Nadia, Jake, Leo, Sarah
Owner of meeting: Morgan  ·  Driver: Sarah (notes + owner-column fill)
Goal: lock the per-signal routing contract for Compass v0.1 so we ship the framework, not a dashboard.

FRAME (5 min)
- Why now: Compass v0.1 is the signal-detection layer; this session decides what each signal triggers, who it lands on, and what travels with it. Without this, signals die in #data or balloon into a board view — both fail modes.
- Out of scope today: pricing, roadmap Q2, board reporting, hiring.
- Rule for the hour: every signal gets one action, one owner column, one audience, one evidence bar, one explicit non-build.

PER-SIGNAL REVIEW (35 min — ~7 min each, owner calls the action)

For each signal below, the group answers in this exact order:
  1. Triggered action (what we do this week, not eventually)
  2. Audience (who is paged / looped; explicit non-audience too)
  3. Evidence + caveat that travel with the signal (one line each)
  4. Account-note / source-quality bar that must be true before it fires
  5. Explicit non-build (the thing we are NOT making because of this signal)

Signals (5):
  S1. Activation reached (aha moment logged, N days post-onboard)
  S2. Usage depth shift (feature breadth or seats trending up/down)
  S3. Expansion readiness (plan/seat/MAD signal)
  S4. Risk / churn risk (engagement drop + sponsor change + support pattern)
  S5. Procurement / security posture (admin audit, cert, SSO posture)

BOUNDARIES — revisit mid-room, not just closing (10 min)
- No board dashboard. Signals route to a person + action, never aggregate up to a KPI view. If Jake needs an investor-grade number, it is derived on-demand, not piped live.
- No new-hiring lane. All routing and follow-through lands on existing Anna/Nadia/Leo/Sarah capacity. If we hit a capacity wall, we cut a signal, not hire for it.
- Jake in the room = product-update lens only. No raw signal feeds, no roadmap speculation, no MAD math beyond what is already shared externally.

DECISIONS + OWNER COLUMN (10 min)
- Fill the owner column for each of the 5 signals. Sarah owns the doc.
- Resolve: which one signal is the v0.1 pilot we ship first, and what is the kill criterion if it underperforms in 30 days.
- Confirm: what we explicitly punt to post-v0.1 (predictive scoring, multi-account rollup, anything that smells like a dashboard).

ARTIFACTS OUT OF THE SESSION
- One updated per-signal row: action / audience / evidence+caveat / source-quality bar / non-build / owner.
- A 5-line "what changed" note for #eng-releases (not #eng-all) — Honeycomb or equivalent evidence required for any shipped signal.
- A 3-line product update suitable for Jake to forward, written in the existing product-update cadence.

PRE-READ (Sarah sends Mon EOD)
- This agenda
- The current Compass signal list with blanks in the 5 columns
- Last session's note (link)

ATTENDEE ROLE MAP (correct before sending)
- Anna — Product (signal semantics, non-build calls)
- Nadia — Eng (source-quality bar, evidence plumbing)
- Jake — Investor-comms gate (product-update read-only; gate to fundraising lane)
- Leo — GTM / CS (triggered action for S3, S4)
- Sarah — Ops (owner column, doc, follow-through)

If your real list differs, swap the names in the "Signals (5)" block and the 7-min cadence still holds.

- No new-hiring lane — routed into "we cut a signal, not hire for it" under Boundaries.
- Jake's lane per memory: investor-comms gate, product updates only; no MAD math, no roadmap speculation in this room.

The 5 questions are in fixed order per signal so the room can't drift: action → audience → evidence+caveat → source-quality bar → explicit non-build. Sarah owns the doc + owner column per "routing: name owner in column; never imply as promise."

arguments.body:
# Offer Prep — Nadia Singh, Head of Customer Growth

**Status: PREP ONLY — held until third-party background verification clears.** This document is not an offer, does not constitute offer approval, and is not a final hiring decision. No communication of terms to candidate until verification returns and Morgan / Devon explicitly approve.

Prepared by: HR
Reviewers: Morgan Chen, Devon Hayes
CC: Sarah Kim
Date drafted: 2024-03-25

---

## 1. Headline (for HR's own tracking, not for candidate)

- Preferred candidate: Nadia Singh
- Role: Head of Customer Growth
- Reports to: Morgan Chen
- Background verification: in progress (third-party); do not proceed until cleared
- Recommended draft band (mid): see §3–§4

## 2. Process posture (must be preserved in any verbal or written handoff)

- Treat the verification as process diligence only.
- Do not communicate compensation, title, start date, or equity to Nadia until:
  1. Background verification returns clean, and
  2. Morgan and Devon explicitly approve moving to verbal / written offer.
- If HR needs to prep paperwork, park it. Do not send.

## 3. Compensation — draft range to model against

HR's proposed range, held for review:

- Title / reporting
  - Head of Customer Growth
  - Reports to Morgan Chen
- Cash comp
  - Base salary band: $245,000 – $265,000
  - Target annual bonus: 20% of base
  - Sign-on: none by default. Up to $20,000 modeled only if used to offset documented forfeited cash or equity from Nadia's current role.
- Equity
  - Initial option grant: 0.60% – 0.80% of fully diluted shares
  - Standard 4-year vest, 1-year cliff

Decision points for Morgan / Devon before draft is finalized:
- [ ] Base salary point within band (and rationale if above midpoint)
- [ ] Bonus target confirmed at 20% (or revised)
- [ ] Sign-on: confirm $0 default; flag only if Nadia surfaces forfeited compensation
- [ ] Equity point within band, including refresh philosophy vs. current exec grants
- [ ] Any one-time relocation or immigration-related cash that needs separate modeling

## 4. Start-date options (held in draft, none communicated yet)

HR will hold all three in the draft template; only one is selected at offer stage:

- Mon Apr 15, 2024
- Mon Apr 22, 2024
- Mon May 6, 2024

Selection criteria to confirm at offer time:
- Nadia's notice-period requirement at current employer
- Background-verification return date
- Internal onboarding capacity (Sarah Kim, Devon Hayes)

## 5. Role scope — first 90 days (working stub for verbal offer / memo)

To be used only after approval; do not share prior:

- Primary focus: turn Mercury and early enterprise-adoption learning into a repeatable customer-growth rhythm
- Internal partnerships
  - Sarah Kim — live-account continuity and pattern capture
  - Devon Hayes — enterprise-readiness packaging and procurement framing
- Explicit non-goals for first 90 days
  - No expectation of building a conventional field-sales org immediately
  - No authority to make bespoke product promises outside approved company priorities
- Success looks like (draft, to be tightened with Morgan / Devon input):
  - [ ] Documented Mercury learnings → repeatable motion
  - [ ] Clear handoff pattern with Sarah for live accounts
  - [ ] Enterprise-readiness and procurement assets in flight with Devon
  - [ ] No out-of-band product commitments made

## 6. Documentation / approvals needed before this becomes an offer

- [ ] Background verification returned clean
- [ ] Morgan Chen approval (verbal OK at minimum; written preferred)
- [ ] Devon Hayes approval
- [ ] Base, bonus, equity, start date, sign-on confirmed against §3–§4
- [ ] Board / compensation-committee notification if required by current grant approvals
- [ ] HR package: offer letter, equity grant agreement, NDA / IP assignment, benefits enrollment, background-check disclosure already on file
- [ ] Communication plan for verbal → written sequence agreed

## 7. What HR will do this week

- Build the offer-letter and equity-grant templates against the midpoint of the bands above, parameterized so the final point can be swapped in.
- Hold all drafts in HR's working folder. Do not route to Nadia, recruiter, or external counsel.
- Once verification clears and approvals land, request a 24-hour turnaround for Morgan / Devon sign-off before any candidate communication.

---

*Reminder: this is parked material. No verbal or written communication of these terms to Nadia until §6 is fully checked.*

ARCHIVE NOTE — 2024 CUSTOMER-GROWTH / GTM LEADER SEARCH
Author: Morgan Chen
Filed: 2026-09-14
Status: archived scope record. Not a current project plan; not a re-opening of the search.

Purpose of this note
-------------------
Capture, on the record, what the 2024 customer-growth/GTM leader search was authorized to do, what the resulting role was scoped to do, and what it explicitly did NOT authorize. Written so a future reader (or a future me) does not have to reconstruct the boundary from scattered emails, and so the role is not retrospectively re-scoped.

Cutoff and references
---------------------
- Search and offer: Feb–Mar 2024.
- Hire start: Apr 15, 2024 (Nadia Singh, Head of Customer Growth).
- 60-day operating read: Jun 14, 2024. Plain operating read shared with Sofia: Jun 18, 2024.
- Source materials used to write this note:
  - HR finalist packet and search calibration, Mar 22, 2024.
  - HR offer-prep range with role-scope stub, Mar 25, 2024.
  - Q1 all-hands framing and employee Q&A, Apr 3, 2024.
  - Sarah Kim / Devon Hayes pre-start packet skeleton, Apr 8, 2024.
  - Q2 plain operating read for Sofia, Jun 18, 2024.

What the search WAS meant to achieve
------------------------------------
1) Fill the one planned post-raise leadership seat. The Series B closed Feb 22, 2024. The post-raise hiring sequence decision named exactly one next new leadership search: a customer-growth / GTM leader. No other leadership lanes were opened at that time.

2) Convert messy design-partner and early-enterprise-adoption learning into a repeatable customer-growth motion. The brief was not a generic enterprise-sales VP role. It was specifically: take founder memory and scattered customer anecdotes, turn them into a small set of repeatable stages, owner handoffs, and leading indicators — without pretending the company was already a fully tooled enterprise vendor.

3) Pair with two existing owners, not replace them.
   - Sarah Kim — live-account continuity and pattern capture.
   - Devon Hayes — enterprise-readiness packaging and procurement framing.
   The new role was scoped as the connective tissue between live accounts and the enterprise-readiness lane, not as a new front door that bypasses either.

4) Report to Morgan. Hiring sequence held by Morgan; Devon and HR only route inside the small reset group unless Morgan reviews.

5) Hire on a boundary judgment calibration. Candidates were screened for: clear differentiation between packaging/clarity work and real roadmap commitments; comfort working without a mature sales org; comfort with technical buyers, implementation friction, and early product gaps; stage fit for "signal but not yet a system." Candidates who drifted into classic enterprise-sales language quickly (territory coverage, comp plans, pipeline mechanics, "what can product commit by quarter-end") were explicitly de-prioritized.

What the search and resulting role did NOT authorize
----------------------------------------------------
1) No bespoke enterprise roadmap brokerage. The role was not defined as opening a route to make per-customer roadmap commitments. The Apr 29, 2024 loop-in to the Evergreen Bank thread was for customer-growth pattern capture only; Sarah remained live-thread continuity owner, Devon remained commercial/procurement owner, and Nadia's involvement did not authorize roadmap promises or change product facts.

2) No conventional field-sales org build. First-90-day scope explicitly stated no expectation of building a conventional field-sales org immediately. As of Jun 14, 2024, Morgan + Devon decided not to open RevOps, CS, SDR, or field-sales lanes in Q3. HR was told to keep the customer-growth org shape quiet until Nadia had two more cadence cycles and the July Evergreen review.

3) No reopening of the second Mercury engineering req. The existing Mercury engineering headcount plan kept the second Mercury engineering hire on hold. Reopen trigger is external launch-readiness feedback from design-partner conversations/trials, not an arbitrary calendar date, and not the existence of the new customer-growth leader.

4) No acceleration implied by the Series B. The Series B did not authorize a broader hiring push. "Hired the planned leader" and "accelerating headcount because we raised" were explicitly separated in the Q2 operating read.

5) No pre-start customer work and no future-team design exercise. Both add-ons in Sarah/Devon's pre-start packet skeleton (a customer-call list and a customer-growth recruiting debrief placeholder) were cut before the packet went to Nadia. The packet was reading/context only — orient to existing Mercury and Evergreen materials and the post-raise owner split, nothing more.

6) No out-of-band product commitments. Product truth stayed separate from later commercial/procurement packaging. The role was authorized to do packaging/clarity work at the level of current constraint, current workaround, and what evidence would change prioritization — not to manufacture certainty.

7) No claim that customer-growth was "fully staffed." As of the Jun 18, 2024 60-day read, cadence was clearly useful but still manual, the input system (account notes) was not clean enough to justify another GTM layer, and Mercury/Evergreen expansion repeatability evidence was still being built. The org shape was on hold pending more cycles and the July Evergreen review.

What the role WAS authorized to do, summarized
---------------------------------------------
- Build a repeatable customer-growth rhythm around Mercury activation, Evergreen-style enterprise-readiness signals, and expansion failure modes.
- Run with Sarah on live-account continuity and pattern capture.
- Run with Devon on enterprise-readiness packaging and procurement framing.
- Produce a weekly read that classifies Mercury/Evergreen signals into: activation friction; admin handoff/role confusion; procurement/security packaging; expansion stalls after first live sync; true product gaps — with an owner route attached to each bucket.
- Stay inside those boundaries for the first 90 days, then revisit org shape based on cadence quality and the July Evergreen review.

What this note is not
--------------------
- Not a re-opening of the search or the role.
- Not a redefinition of the role's scope.
- Not a current project plan.
- Not a critique of the hire. The hire was on-calibration and the boundaries held.

If this note ever conflicts with later 2024–2026 operating decisions, the later decisions govern — but the original scope should remain visible here so the boundary is not silently rewritten.

3) Pair with two existing owners, not replace them.
   - Sarah Kim — live-account continuity and pattern capture.
   - Devon Hayes — enterprise-readiness packaging and procurement framing.
   The new role was scoped as the connective tissue between live accounts and the enterprise-readiness lane, not as a new front door that bypasses either.

4) Report to Morgan. Hiring sequence held by Morgan; Devon and HR only route inside the small reset group unless Morgan reviews.

5) Hire on a boundary judgment calibration. Candidates were screened for: clear differentiation between packaging/clarity work and real roadmap commitments; comfort working without a mature sales org; comfort with technical buyers, implementation friction, and early product gaps; stage fit for "signal but not yet a system." Candidates who drifted into classic enterprise-sales language quickly (territory coverage, comp plans, pipeline mechanics, "what can product commit by quarter-end") were explicitly de-prioritized.

What the search and resulting role did NOT authorize
----------------------------------------------------
1) No bespoke enterprise roadmap brokerage. The role was not defined as opening a route to make per-customer roadmap commitments. The Apr 29, 2024 loop-in to the Evergreen Bank thread was for customer-growth pattern capture only; Sarah remained live-thread continuity owner, Devon remained commercial/procurement owner, and Nadia's involvement did not authorize roadmap promises or change product facts.

2) No conventional field-sales org build. First-90-day scope explicitly stated no expectation of building a conventional field-sales org immediately. As of Jun 14, 2024, Morgan + Devon decided not to open RevOps, CS, SDR, or field-sales lanes in Q3. HR was told to keep the customer-growth org shape quiet until Nadia had two more cadence cycles and the July Evergreen review.

3) No reopening of the second Mercury engineering req. The existing Mercury engineering headcount plan kept the second Mercury engineering hire on hold. Reopen trigger is external launch-readiness feedback from design-partner conversations/trials, not an arbitrary calendar date, and not the existence of the new customer-growth leader.

4) No acceleration implied by the Series B. The Series B did not authorize a broader hiring push. "Hired the planned leader" and "accelerating headcount because we raised" were explicitly separated in the Q2 operating read.

5) No pre-start customer work and no future-team design exercise. Both add-ons in Sarah/Devon's pre-start packet skeleton (a customer-call list and a customer-growth recruiting debrief placeholder) were cut before the packet went to Nadia. The packet was reading/context only — orient to existing Mercury and Evergreen materials and the post-raise owner split, nothing more.

6) No out-of-band product commitments. Product truth stayed separate from later commercial/procurement packaging. The role was authorized to do packaging/clarity work at the level of current constraint, current workaround, and what evidence would change prioritization — not to manufacture certainty.

7) No claim that customer-growth was "fully staffed." As of the Jun 18, 2024 60-day read, cadence was clearly useful but still manual, the input system (account notes) was not clean enough to justify another GTM layer, and Mercury/Evergreen expansion repeatability evidence was still being built. The org shape was on hold pending more cycles and the July Evergreen review.

What the role WAS authorized to do, summarized
---------------------------------------------
- Build a repeatable customer-growth rhythm around Mercury activation, Evergreen-style enterprise-readiness signals, and expansion failure modes.
- Run with Sarah on live-account continuity and pattern capture.
- Run with Devon on enterprise-readiness packaging and procurement framing.
- Produce a weekly read that classifies Mercury/Evergreen signals into: activation friction; admin handoff/role confusion; procurement/security packaging; expansion stalls after first live sync; true product gaps — with an owner route attached to each bucket.
- Stay inside those boundaries for the first 90 days, then revisit org shape based on cadence quality and the July Evergreen review.

What this note is not
--------------------
- Not a re-opening of the search or the role.
- Not a redefinition of the role's scope.
- Not a current project plan.
- Not a critique of the hire. The hire was on-calibration and the boundaries held.

If this note ever conflicts with later 2024–2026 operating decisions, the later decisions govern — but the original scope should remain visible here so the boundary is not silently rewritten.

Title: Northstar diligence — retention methodology note (September / October Mercury cohorts)

Purpose
This note stays on the existing September / October 2023 external Mercury cohort package. It does not introduce a broader pipeline view, weekly operating cuts, or sample-preview diagnostics.

1) Cohort construction / scope
For the September and October 2023 external cohorts, 'entered the bounded Mercury flow' means an account entered the current bounded Mercury setup path used in the external package: invited into the product, able to access by the current invite / magic-link path, able to interact with preview-only sample data if present, and then progress toward connecting a real source and completing a first live sync. The construction is intentionally limited to that bounded Mercury flow and does not widen into a broader top-of-funnel or sales-pipeline view.

2) Activation definition
For the outside-reader view, activated within 7 days means that within the first seven days after entering the bounded Mercury flow, the account either:
- connected a real source, or
- completed a first live sync.

The following do not count as activation:
- sample import / preview-only behavior
- invite sent
- invite accepted
- preview viewed
- source selected in-product
- similar first-week motion that does not reach real-source connection or first live sync

3) October 19/27 versus 16/27
In the October 2023 cohort, 19 of 27 accounts were activated within 7 days and 16 of 27 completed first live sync within 7 days. The full gap between those two numbers is 3 accounts that connected a real source within 7 days but did not complete first live sync in that same seven-day window.

There is no additional preview-only, invite-only, or source-selected-only state inside the activation numerator.

4) Expansion / longer-window caveat
The external package stays week-one focused because that is the defensible read from the current September / October cohort set. The improved signal is that more accounts are getting through the first-admin path to real-source connection and, from there, into first live sync inside the first seven days.

Weekly cuts, sample-preview diagnostics, and similar operating views remain internal only. They are not the board / investor view and are not being added to this confirmatory package.

Now I have a clear picture of what's actually in the record. I want to be straight with you before I make anything.

What I found:
- The session archive has zero direct trace of a March 13, 2023 planning document listing proposed Q3 workstreams and cross-team operating leads. That date falls inside a stretch where session records are sparse, and the only relevant hits are indirect — references to a "Volkov retention arc," a "mid-Volkov Q3 push," and Anna Martinez starting 2023-03-13.
- Anna Martinez actually started 2023-03-13 (retention-data lead, reporting to Devon, joining mid-Volkov Q3 push). So the date itself isn't invented — but that single fact doesn't license me to invent a list of Q3 workstreams and operating leads around it.
- Memory notes a "Q3 = real push" framing and Devon "on deck" for the deck work — that's the extent of what's grounded.

A planning archive note dated 2023-03-13 that names specific proposed workstreams and a cross-team operating lead requires you to actually have been considering those things on that date. I don't have that record. If I write the note from scratch, I'd be inventing the workstreams and the lead's name — and putting it in an archive under a specific historical date is exactly the kind of thing that quietly becomes "real" later.

Two ways to go, and I'd rather ask than guess:

1. You have the actual list from March 2023 somewhere (an old doc, a Slack thread, your notes, a screenshot, a Loom). Share even a fragment and I'll archive it faithfully — names, workstreams, lead, status as of that date.
2. You want me to reconstruct from what IS grounded (Volkov retention arc, Anna starting that day, Devon's role, the Q3-push framing, the Mercury context) and label it explicitly as a reconstruction, not a contemporaneous note. I can do that with the lead role written as "considered / not finalized" so it doesn't get read as a decision.

Which do you want? If (2), I'll write it now with a clear "reconstructed from memory fragments, not a verbatim 2023-03-13 doc" header and keep every lead name and workstream tied to something the record actually supports. If (1), send whatever you have and I'll archive it cleanly.

Saturday, December 23, 2023 → Monday, January 1, 2024.
Normal schedule resumed Tuesday, January 2, 2024.

Source: HR coverage package finalized Dec 20, 2023
(alternate founder escalation line + Option B meeting posture),
confirmed in DMs to Marcus on Dec 21 and Dec 26.


1. THRESHOLDS
- No threshold changes for the window. Existing Honeycomb alert
  rules stayed as-is. No mid-holiday tuning.
- Rationale (recorded at the time): avoid alert-rule churn while
  coverage is thin; hold noise floor steady so any real signal is
  visible against the baseline.

- First page goes to the named on-call owner, every time.
- Engineering on-call / production — primary: Marcus;
  backup: Leo Park.
- The on-call owner owns the acknowledgment. No auto-escalation
  past the named owner on timer alone.

Two triggers only. Both must be true before paging Morgan:
  (a) confirmed customer impact, or
  (b) owner unreachable after the documented ack/rotation path
      is exhausted.

window. Founders are not the catch-all.

- If the week stays quiet (no page, no escalation triggers met),
  alerts roll into Monday's digest instead of paging.
- Mid-window reduced-week digest (Dec 26, Marcus) used this exact
  shape: count of non-prod flaps, count of slow acks, confirmation
  of no confirmed customer impact. That digest format carried
  through the rest of the break.

- Two non-prod alert flaps — recorded, no customer impact,
  parked for Monday digest, no tuning action.
- One slow acknowledgment — recorded, no escalation trigger met,
  parked for Monday digest.

- No mid-holiday threshold changes.
- Non-urgent cleanup (rule tuning, flap follow-up, ack-SLO review)
  deferred to January.

- Review the two non-prod flap signatures once normal staffing is

- No tuning action taken during the window itself.


NOTES
- Standing rule not spelled out in the Dec 23 coverage announcement
  but in force during the window: no prod pushes after Fri 3pm
  without a full on-call roster. Deploy authority chain for the
  window was Devon Hayes (P) / Marcus (B).
- Channel for the digests: internal team chat (Slack), DM to
  Marcus as the on-call lead; Morgan only on the two triggers above.
- This is a historical reconstruction from the Dec 20 coverage
  package and the Dec 21 / Dec 26 DMs to Marcus. No threshold
  values, alert names, or SLO numbers are reconstructed — those
  were the existing rules at the time and were held unchanged.

arguments.title: Leo Park — Mercury onboarding brief
arguments.body:
For: Sarah Kim (HR) and manager handoff
Start date: Monday, July 10, 2023
Role: Mercury engineering, joining the launch-readiness pod

First-week emphasis
- Mercury release discipline, end-to-end. Not a generic "ramp on the codebase" week.
  Leo should leave week 1 fluent in how a Mercury release actually ships: the
  pipeline path, the release-notes channel rule (#eng-releases, never
  #eng-all), the Friday 3pm prod-push gate, and what "post-launch readiness"
  looks like in practice.
- Platform seams. Where Mercury ends and the rest of the stack begins:
  Honeycomb for observability (canonical — not Datadog), Clerk for auth
  (Rishi is still integrating, so this is in-flight, not stable), and the
  mchen-notes-v3 vector namespace for canonical notes. Older namespaces are
  stale — he should not query them.
- Launch readiness for Q3 Mercury. Treat week 1 as an orientation into the
  actual July launch checklist, not a sandbox. Shadow the deploy process,
  read the last two release notes, and sit in on the next pre-green review.

Immediate scope to drop him into
- Shadow the next Mercury release through pipeline → pre-green → ship.
- Own one small launch-readiness task by end of week 1 (size-scoped, not
  a feature — e.g. a Honeycomb dashboard check or a release-notes draft).
- Read: the Mercury weekly operating note template, the last two release
  notes, and the current Q3 launch checklist.

Pair-with order, first week
1. Jake — operating cadence, Mercury weekly note format, current launch
   blockers. Jake owns the Mercury operating note; Leo should understand
   the format before he contributes.
2. Priya — activation/onboarding UX context for Mercury through Q3 launch.
   She owns the activation surface Leo's work will sit next to.
3. Marcus — platform seams. Auth (Clerk) integration state, observability
   (Honeycomb), deploy path. Where Mercury hands off to the rest of the
   stack.

Handoff points
- From Jake: Mercury operating note ownership context; what "activation
  blocker" and "admin blocker" mean in the weekly format; current open
  items on his list Leo should pick up.
- From Priya: current activation UX state, what shipped vs. what's
  queued, and where Leo's engineering work will touch her surface.
- From Marcus: Clerk integration status and the seam points Leo needs to
  know before he writes code that crosses the platform boundary.

Do NOT force the second Mercury engineering hire before July
launch-readiness feedback
- We have one Mercury eng hire landing (Leo). The plan had been to move
  on a second hire quickly, but the explicit call is: do not start that
  search, do not extend an offer, and do not backfill the req until we
  have Leo's first-month feedback on launch readiness and we have shipped
  the July Mercury release. Reasoning: a second hire pulled in before
  launch-readiness signal would either be mis-scoped or would pull Leo's
  onboarding attention. Revisit after the July launch retro.

Packet tone note for HR
- This is not a standard engineering template. Frame it as "you're joining
  a product pod mid-launch, here's the actual work." Avoid generic
  "meet everyone / ramp on the codebase" framing in the packet itself.

arguments.title: Mercury / Evergreen Bank — procurement packet (final)
arguments.body:
# Mercury — Procurement & Security Review Packet

Prepared for: Evergreen Bank
Date: September 13, 2023
Prepared by: Morgan Chen, Co-Founder & CEO, Scaffold
Commercial / procurement owner: Devon Hayes
Document version: v1.0 (final for procurement/security review)

---

## 1. Purpose

This packet gives Evergreen Bank's procurement and security teams a written summary of the current Mercury product so the bounded design-partner deployment can be reviewed asynchronously. It covers the commercial model, the present login and setup scope, the current admin and security posture for the bounded launch experience, and the enterprise-readiness items that are not part of the live launch.

This packet is intended to stand on its own. It is not a roadmap commitment.

## 2. Commercial model

Mercury is priced on monthly active developer usage. It is not priced per purchased seat and is not tied to directory size.

Standard pricing bands:

- Pilot: $2,500 / month platform minimum, including up to 50 monthly active developers
- Growth: $7,500 / month platform minimum, including up to 200 monthly active developers
- Overage: $1,000 per additional block of 50 monthly active developers

Counting rules:

- Monthly active developer usage is the pricing driver.
- Scaffold internal users and test users do not count toward usage.
- Preview and sample-only behavior is distinct from activation reporting and is not treated as a usage proof on its own.

Billing cadence and payment terms are covered in the standard order form.

## 3. Current Mercury scope

The current Mercury design-partner experience is the live bounded experience now in use. It includes:

- Clerk-backed sessions
- Magic-link sign-in
- Org invites
- A setup flow oriented around connecting a real source
- Preview and sample data, available as preview behavior only and not activating the account on its own
- First live sync path in product

Current activation definition (for operating review only):

- real_source_connected within 7 days, or
- first_live_sync_completed within 7 days

Items not in current launch scope:

- SSO
- Audit history for admin changes
- Expanded enterprise / security packaging beyond the current design-partner flow
- Deeper admin controls beyond what is present in the current bounded experience

## 4. Current login and setup experience

User access for the present Mercury flow is handled through magic links and org invites. Session handling is Clerk-backed.

Intended path:

1. Invited user enters through the magic link / invite flow
2. User lands in the Mercury workspace context
3. User connects a real source
4. User reaches first live sync

Preview and sample behavior may be shown during evaluation, but preview/sample-only behavior does not activate the account and should not be described as equivalent to a real source connection or a live sync completion.

## 5. Current admin and security posture for the present scope

Current readiness should be read as sufficient for the bounded design-partner experience, not as a full enterprise admin and security package.

Statements that are accurate for the present scope:

- Access is handled through the current magic-link and invite flow
- Org-level invitation exists in the current Mercury experience
- The launch experience is intentionally narrower than a full enterprise rollout
- Current product facts should be reviewed against the present scope, not against a broader enterprise-control checklist

Statements this packet does not make:

- That Mercury currently includes full enterprise-ready login controls
- That current admin behavior covers all enterprise audit and control requirements
- That later-scope items are part of the live launch package

## 6. Known enterprise-readiness gaps

The following items are open follow-up work. They are not part of the current Mercury launch scope and are not included in the present packet as available features.

- Single sign-on (SSO)
- Audit history for admin changes
- Clearer separation between admin permissions and billing-owner controls
- Procurement and security material that can be reviewed end-to-end without a live walkthrough

These items are roadmap-dependent. They will be quoted as available only after they ship.

## 7. Document ownership

- Commercial / procurement owner: Devon Hayes (devon@scaffold.dev)
- Executive sponsor: Morgan Chen, Co-Founder & CEO, Scaffold (morgan@scaffold.dev)
- Product / engineering appendix owner: Jake (internal)

Security and procurement reviewers at Evergreen Bank can direct follow-up questions on this packet to Devon Hayes.

input.body:
Correction on the June 8, 2023 auth readout:

The June 8, 2023 readout did **not** choose a provider and did **not** approve production. That framing is wrong; please update.

What the June 8, 2023 readout actually established:
  - The team narrowed the shortlist and aligned on evaluation criteria (security posture, SDK ergonomics, hosted/on-prem fit, observability, cost-at-our-trajectory).
  - A side-by-side comparison of the remaining candidates was presented, but no winner was named — two candidates were still effectively tied on weighted criteria.
  - Open questions were captured, not closed: data-residency for EU customers, session-lifetime semantics, our existing identity/admin model, and the path for staged rollout behind a flag.

What was unresolved and had to happen next (in this order):
  1. A targeted proof-of-concept on the tied candidates against a real Scaffold tenant, including a hostile-token test and a load profile at 2x current peak.
  2. Legal/security review of the candidate's data-processing terms and sub-processor list, with a written sign-off.
  3. A spike on migration: how to dual-run, how to back out, and how existing sessions/tokens are handled during cutover.
  4. A staged-rollout plan with kill-switch and metrics, reviewed by eng + on-call before any production traffic.
  5. Only then: a decision (still pending as of June 8), and only after that, a separate, explicit production approval — not implicit from the readout.

Net: June 8, 2023 ended with a shortlist and a punch list, not a decision and not production approval.

arguments.title: Leo Park — Mercury onboarding brief
arguments.body:
For: Sarah Kim (HR) and manager handoff
Start date: Monday, July 10, 2023
Role: Mercury engineering, joining the launch-readiness pod

First-week emphasis
- Mercury release discipline, end-to-end. Not a generic "ramp on the codebase" week.
  Leo should leave week 1 fluent in how a Mercury release actually ships: the
  pipeline path, the release-notes channel rule (#eng-releases, never
  #eng-all), the Friday 3pm prod-push gate, and what "post-launch readiness"
  looks like in practice.
- Platform seams. Where Mercury ends and the rest of the stack begins:
  Honeycomb for observability (canonical — not Datadog), Clerk for auth
  (Rishi is still integrating, so this is in-flight, not stable), and the
  mchen-notes-v3 vector namespace for canonical notes. Older namespaces are
  stale — he should not query them.
- Launch readiness for Q3 Mercury. Treat week 1 as an orientation into the
  actual July launch checklist, not a sandbox. Shadow the deploy process,
  read the last two release notes, and sit in on the next pre-green review.

Immediate scope to drop him into
- Shadow the next Mercury release through pipeline → pre-green → ship.
- Own one small launch-readiness task by end of week 1 (size-scoped, not
  a feature — e.g. a Honeycomb dashboard check or a release-notes draft).
- Read: the Mercury weekly operating note template, the last two release
  notes, and the current Q3 launch checklist.

Pair-with order, first week
1. Jake — operating cadence, Mercury weekly note format, current launch
   blockers. Jake owns the Mercury operating note; Leo should understand
   the format before he contributes.
2. Priya — activation/onboarding UX context for Mercury through Q3 launch.
   She owns the activation surface Leo's work will sit next to.
3. Marcus — platform seams. Auth (Clerk) integration state, observability
   (Honeycomb), deploy path. Where Mercury hands off to the rest of the
   stack.

Handoff points
- From Jake: Mercury operating note ownership context; what "activation
  blocker" and "admin blocker" mean in the weekly format; current open
  items on his list Leo should pick up.
- From Priya: current activation UX state, what shipped vs. what's
  queued, and where Leo's engineering work will touch her surface.
- From Marcus: Clerk integration status and the seam points Leo needs to
  know before he writes code that crosses the platform boundary.

Do NOT force the second Mercury engineering hire before July
launch-readiness feedback
- We have one Mercury eng hire landing (Leo). The plan had been to move
  on a second hire quickly, but the explicit call is: do not start that
  search, do not extend an offer, and do not backfill the req until we
  have Leo's first-month feedback on launch readiness and we have shipped
  the July Mercury release. Reasoning: a second hire pulled in before
  launch-readiness signal would either be mis-scoped or would pull Leo's
  onboarding attention. Revisit after the July launch retro.

Packet tone note for HR
- This is not a standard engineering template. Frame it as "you're joining
  a product pod mid-launch, here's the actual work." Avoid generic
  "meet everyone / ramp on the codebase" framing in the packet itself.

Historical onboarding note. Drafted 2026-09-14 from the original June 2023 onboarding brief and the July 2023 ramp plan.

Context
- Leo Park signed 2023-06-22; July 10, 2023 start date.
- Joined as Staff Engineer, Mercury pod, mid Q3 launch ramp.
- Second Mercury engineering hire deliberately on hold pending his first-month signal; revisit tied to launch-readiness feedback, not the old two-senior plan.

First-month focus
- Mercury release discipline end-to-end: pipeline path, #eng-releases channel rule, Friday 3pm prod-push gate, what "post-launch readiness" actually means.
- Platform seams: Honeycomb (canonical observability, not Datadog), Clerk auth (in-flight, Rishi integrating), mchen-notes-v3 vector namespace for canonical notes. Older namespaces are stale — don't query them.
- Launch readiness for Q3 Mercury. Week 1 is orientation into the actual July launch checklist, not sandbox.
- Pair order: Jake (operating cadence, Mercury weekly note format, current launch blockers), Priya (activation/onboarding UX context for Mercury), Marcus (Clerk integration state, observability, deploy path).
- Own one small launch-readiness task by end of week 1 (e.g. a Honeycomb dashboard check or a release-notes draft), not a feature.

Expected first output
- A release-risk readout grounded in evidence: where launch risk is actually hiding, what is still thin, and what needs one more direct check before wider dogfood / launch decisions.
- Not abstract platform recommendations. Not a rewrite plan.
- Inputs feeding it: Jake's Mercury weekly (blockers, evidence, decisions, owner gaps — the operating spine), Priya's Figma source-of-truth path for activation/onboarding, and Marcus's release-readiness / thin-evidence discipline.
- Leo is expected to be skeptical of "we saw it once in staging" and to distinguish repeated-evidence behavior from demo-only or under-proven behavior.

Framing note
- Leo was framed in onboarding as joining a product pod mid-launch, not a generic engineering ramp. The readout is the artifact that proves the framing landed.

arguments.title: Acme — Mercury wave + NDA boundary (internal)
arguments.body:
Internal — not for Greg. Do not send the holding reply until reviewed.

Context
- Greg Shipman (Acme) reopened the NDA/design-partner thread on 2023-06-15. Two asks bundled:
  1. Acme should be in the first Mercury design-partner wave, not treated as a fresh account — wants a direct yes/no.
  2. NDA should cover the underlying evaluation materials, not only polished/customer-facing assets. Asks for written examples of what falls outside if we disagree.
- Per Morgan's instruction: do not settle design-partner status today; do not itemize NDA carve-outs in a way that creates a new mess.

Known gaps (need answers before any reply leaves)
- I could not locate the prior Acme NDA thread or any prior internal statement of Scaffold's NDA boundary in this session. Search returned no hits; inbox is empty. Treating prior thread as unknown — not safe to claim continuity I cannot verify.
- "First Mercury design-partner wave" — definition, criteria, and current candidate list are not visible to me here. Jake owns the Mercury operating note (per profile); the wave definition likely lives there or in a Product doc I haven't read. Do not commit to a slot, a sequence, or a "later" trigger condition until that's confirmed.

Holding reply — DO NOT SEND
Goals: acknowledge both asks, defer the wave decision without naming Acme's status, hold the NDA line, refuse to itemize examples.
Channel: email, reply on Greg's thread.
Tone: short, plain, not warm, not cold. Matches Greg's directness without conceding anything.

Subject: Re: Mercury design-partner wave / NDA coverage

Greg,

Thanks for putting both points in one place — easier to handle.

On the design-partner wave: I'm not going to settle Acme's status in this reply. We're still finalizing the shape and criteria for the first wave internally, and I'd rather give you a real answer than a placeholder. I'll come back to you once that's set; if it helps, I can give you a rough timeline for that decision in the next few days.

On the NDA scope: our position is that confidentiality covers the materials we share with you under the agreement, including the underlying evaluation content. We are not going to enumerate categories that fall outside the scope — doing so tends to create exactly the kind of ambiguity the NDA is meant to avoid, and that wouldn't serve either side. If a specific item comes up, flag it and we'll address it concretely.

Morgan

Why each line is there
- "Not going to settle Acme's status in this reply" — direct, no-spin, avoids both "yes" and the worse "maybe later with conditions" that Greg explicitly asked us not to do.
- "Rough timeline in the next few days" — small concession so Greg isn't left cold; does not bind us to a date.
- "We are not going to enumerate categories" — refuses the itemized carve-out Greg requested, per instruction. The "tend to create exactly the kind of ambiguity" line is the substantive reason and is safe to put on the record.
- "Flag it and we'll address it concretely" — keeps the door open for case-by-case without us drawing the line in writing.

Risks / things to watch
- Greg asked specifically for written examples of what falls outside. We are declining that. He may push back; that's expected. Do not soften in the next round — softening is how the carve-out list gets built by accretion.
- If the wave definition does come back as "Acme is in" or "Acme is out," that needs its own clean message, not a tacked-on line at the end of an NDA reply.

[2025-01-17T10:42:00-08:00] These are my kickoff notes for Project Compass, the Scaffold product/operating project to make our internal customer-health signals useful in customer-facing and customer-growth work. Please turn them into a tight internal owner-routing note so the team understands Compass without reading it as a new hiring lane or another board-dashboard project.

Project Compass kickoff notes
Date: January 17, 2025
Participants: Morgan Chen, Anna Martinez, Nadia Singh, Jake, Leo Park, Sarah Kim

Purpose of the meeting
- Name the next operating/product push before the January work turns into separate account threads, Mercury cleanup, and board shorthand.
- Use the signals Scaffold already has from internal operating work, but make them useful to customers and customer-growth follow-up instead of turning them into another internal reporting layer.

Working project name
- Project Compass

Why now
- We already have real signal categories showing up in Mercury/Evergreen work.
- The current-state Evergreen packet exists, so enterprise-readiness can be handled as actual evidence instead of vague sales language.
- The team does not want another board dashboard that looks clean internally but does not change what happens in an account.

Project intent
- Turn internal customer-health signals into customer-facing and customer-success/customer-growth follow-up that changes account behavior.
- The point is not to score accounts for internal consumption only.
- The point is to make the signal lead to a next action, better follow-up, or better customer-facing guidance.

Signals currently available from internal operating use
- Retention
- Activation
- Expansion
- Admin friction
- Enterprise readiness
- Account-note quality

Boundary / what Compass is not
- Do not build another board dashboard.
- Do not treat the first version as investor packaging.
- Do not turn this into a generic health-score project.
- Do not let it become a bespoke Evergreen side track.
- Do not use Compass as a reason to open a new hiring lane.
- Stay with the current lightweight staffing model.

Discussion notes

Morgan
- The framing should stay operational and customer-real, not presentation-ready.
- If Compass becomes a prettier internal dashboard, we missed the point.
- Board narrative matters later, but the first job is to make the signals produce better customer behavior and better follow-up.
- Keep the naming clean now so the work does not fragment into separate Mercury, Evergreen, and customer-growth side conversations.

Anna
- Signal definitions need caveats or they will get over-read immediately.
- “Renewal risk” can easily collapse together very different things: actual product weakness, admin handoff confusion, procurement packaging, or ordinary activation drag.
- Admin friction should not be treated as a churn prediction label by default.
- Every Compass signal needs source evidence attached, plus caveats about what the signal does and does not mean.
- Account-note quality is not separate housekeeping; it changes whether any of the other signals are trustworthy.

Nadia
- Useful only if the signal changes follow-up behavior.
- Customer-growth use cases need owner routing, not just visibility.
- A signal without a next action turns into an FYI bucket and then dies.
- The useful categories still look similar to what worked in the earlier Mercury/Evergreen read: activation friction, admin handoff/role confusion, procurement/security packaging, expansion stalls after first live sync, and true product gaps. Compass should preserve that logic instead of flattening everything into one score.
- Need follow-up that distinguishes evidence from inference so customer-facing outreach does not sound made up.

Jake
- Keep v0.1 narrow enough that it can actually ship or be tested.
- If Compass starts asking for a big new product surface immediately, it will collide with Mercury work and stall.
- Initial product implementation should bias toward lightweight prompts, account workflow support, or a contained product assist rather than a broad new system.
- Anything that drifts into broad admin-policy product or general enterprise-controls work should be called out and kept separate.

Leo
- Data/platform seams need to stay light at first.
- Reuse existing signals and existing event paths where possible.
- Avoid building a separate scoring service or new platform layer just to make the project feel substantial.
- The seam question is: what is the minimum evidence bundle that can move from internal read to customer/action use without breaking trust?
- Need clear boundaries between usage evidence, account-note evidence, and inferred account state.

Sarah
- Current thread notes still mix customer quote, internal interpretation, support follow-up, and procurement context too easily.
- If account-note source quality stays messy, customer-growth follow-up will inherit the confusion.
- Need notes to say what came from the customer directly, what came from usage/readout, and what is internal interpretation.
- Hygiene work matters here because otherwise Compass will look more certain than the underlying record actually is.

Initial v0.1 scope
1. Renewal-risk/admin-friction evidence
- Build a first pass that can show when apparent renewal risk is actually admin friction, setup-control issues, or role confusion.
- Evidence should travel with the signal.
- Avoid binary risk labeling without context.

2. Expansion prompts after first live sync
- Focus on the post-first-live-sync moment.
- Identify what follow-up or prompt should happen after an account reaches first live sync and looks ready for broader usage.
- This is about timely action, not generic upsell language.

3. Cleaner account-note source quality for customer-growth follow-up
- Improve note quality enough that follow-up is based on traceable evidence.
- Source quality should distinguish customer statement, observed usage, support-derived fact, and internal inference.
- Recency and provenance matter.

Owner split
- Anna Martinez owns signal definitions and caveats.
- Nadia Singh owns customer-growth and customer-success use cases.
- Jake owns product implementation and sequencing.
- Leo Park owns data/platform seams.
- Sarah Kim supplies account-thread hygiene.
- Morgan Chen owns board/customer narrative.

Staffing boundary
- Use the current lightweight staffing model.
- Do not open a new hiring lane for Compass.
- Keep the work inside the existing Nadia/Sarah operating model plus Jake/Leo implementation support.

Rough success test for v0.1
- A signal should trigger a clearer next action.
- The recipient should know why they are seeing it.
- The evidence and caveat should travel with it.
- The signal should improve follow-up quality rather than just improve internal visibility.

Open questions captured in the room
- What is the minimum evidence package that has to travel with each signal?
- Which signals should surface only internally first, and which can become customer-facing quickly?
- What is the smallest useful post-first-live-sync expansion prompt?
- How should admin friction be distinguished from true product gaps and from procurement/security packaging?
- What account-note fields or source tags are required before Nadia can trust a follow-up?
- How much Leo seam work is acceptable before Compass starts stealing too much attention from Mercury?

Immediate takeaways
- Compass is real and named.
- v0.1 stays narrow.
- No board-dashboard build.
- No investor-packaging framing.
- No new hiring lane.
- Owners are clear enough to proceed with a lightweight first pass.

PROJECT COMPASS — OWNER ROUTING NOTE (v0.1)
Jan 17, 2025 · Morgan Chen

WHAT
    Turn customer-health signals we already see in Mercury/Evergreen
    internal operating work into routed, actionable signals for the
    person who can act on the account — not another internal-only score.

WHY NOW
    Real signals are already showing up across Mercury, Evergreen, and
    customer-growth work. Without naming it, they fragment into separate
    threads and turn into another internal dashboard that does not
    change account behavior.

WHAT COMPASS IS NOT
    Not a board dashboard. Not investor packaging. Not a generic
    health-score. Not a bespoke Evergreen side-track. Not a reason to
    open a new hiring lane.

v0.1 SCOPE (narrow on purpose)

  1. Renewal-risk evidence pack
     Distinguish admin friction / setup-control / role confusion from
     true product gaps. Evidence + caveats travel with the signal —
     no binary risk labels.

  2. Expansion prompt after first live sync
     Specific to the "just went live and looks ready for broader usage"
     moment. Timely, actionable — not generic upsell language.

  3. Account-note source quality
     Tag each note by source (customer quote / usage observation /
     support-derived / internal inference) + recency. Follow-up inherits
     the evidence trail.

OWNERS
    Anna Martinez — signal definitions + caveats
    Nadia Singh   — customer-growth / CS use cases + routing signals
                    to action owners
    Jake          — product implementation + sequencing (lean; prompts,
                    workflow assist, no broad new surface)
    Leo Park      — data/platform seams (reuse existing events; no new
                    scoring service)
    Sarah Kim     — account-thread hygiene (source tags, provenance)
    Morgan Chen   — board / customer narrative, later

STAFFING
    Current Nadia/Sarah operating model + Jake/Leo implementation
    support. No new headcount for Compass.

SUCCESS TEST FOR v0.1
    Signal triggers a clearer next action.
    Recipient knows why they are seeing it.
    Evidence + caveat travel with it.
    Improves follow-up quality, not just internal visibility.

OPEN QUESTIONS (capture, don't resolve here)
    Minimum evidence bundle per signal (incl. account-note source tags)?
    Which signals stay internal-only vs. surface customer-facing quickly?
    Smallest useful post-first-live-sync expansion prompt?
    How to separate admin friction from true product gap from
    procurement/security packaging?
    How much Leo seam work before this pulls attention from Mercury?

STATUS
    Owners are clear enough to proceed with a lightweight first pass.
